definition_zh: 威胁；恐吓；危及；预示凶险
definition_en: to say that you will harm someone, to put someone or something in danger, or to seem about to do something bad
core_image: 天边推过来一整片乌云，压得人抬不起头
scene: 堤坝上的水位一夜涨了三尺,守夜人不停往村里打电话。 The rising flood threatened the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 threaten 是「危及、威胁到」（第 2 个义项：使某事处于危险中）；句意为上涨的洪水危及整个村庄。

collocations.zh: 威胁要做某事；眼看就要……

derivatives.zh: 由动词去掉后缀 -en 得到的名词，义为「威胁；危险」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；凶险的」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受到威胁的；濒危的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「威胁地」

senses.title: To say you will harm someone
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will hurt them or cause trouble unless they do what you want
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方若不听命就会伤害他或制造麻烦
senses.example: The caller threatened to publish the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 打电话的人威胁说要公布那些照片。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: pressure is applied out loud, before any blow.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：压力在拳头落下之前就大喊着施加出来。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to be likely to harm someone or something, of a thing rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 指事物而非人可能造成伤害
senses.example: Smoke from the factory threatens the health of nearby residents.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的烟危及附近居民的健康。
senses.why: Pressure need not come from a voice; a flood or a policy presses in just as hard.
senses.whyCN: 压力不必来自声音；洪水或政策压得同样沉。

senses.title: To seem about to happen
senses.definition: to look as if something bad is going to happen, of clouds, events or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 指乌云、事件或局势看起来即将发生坏事
senses.example: Dark clouds threatened rain all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午乌云都预示着一场雨。
senses.why: The verb lets an inanimate thing lean forward: the sky itself seems to be pressing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词让无生命之物也前倾身体：连天空看起来都在施压。

senses.title: To endanger an institution or system
senses.definition: to put the continued existence of an organisation, system or custom at risk
senses.definitionCN: 使组织、制度或习俗的存续面临风险
senses.example: The cuts threaten the future of the local library.
senses.exampleCN: 这些削减让本地图书馆的未来岌岌可危。
senses.why: Once anything can press, the passive follows easily: a library, a language or a job can be threatened.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何事物都能施压，被动式便顺理成章：图书馆、语言或工作都能处于威胁之下。

intro.en: Threaten is the verb made from the noun threat with the Germanic suffix -en, which also makes widen and strengthen.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词 threat 加日耳曼语后缀 -en 构成的动词，widen、strengthen 也是同样的做法。

items.en: The old root meant to press or crowd, the pressure behind both threat and throng.
items.cn: 古老词根意为「压、挤」，威胁与 throng 背后的压迫感同源。

items.en: Old English had a verb of the same shape meaning to press or force, alongside the noun for a crowd and for compulsion.
items.cn: 古英语已有同形动词表示「压迫、胁迫」，与表示人群和强制的名词并存。

items.en: Middle English rebuilt the verb on the noun with -en, and threaten came to mean uttering harm or showing danger.
items.cn: 中古英语以名词为词基加 -en 重造动词，threaten 遂表示「扬言伤害」或「显露危险」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb extended to things: clouds, storms and diseases could threaten.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个动词扩展到事物：乌云、风暴与疾病都能 threaten。

items.en: Modern English uses the passive freely, so a species can be threatened with extinction.
items.cn: 现代英语大量使用被动式，于是可以说某个物种面临灭绝的威胁。

note.en: The first group gathers the threat family; the second compares verbs of menacing and warning.
note.cn: 第一组收 threat 词族；第二组比较表示威胁与警告的动词。

entries.definition: The noun, a warning of harm or a source of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「威胁；危险」

entries.definition: The adjective for a menacing look, letter or sky.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「威胁的、凶险的」

entries.definition: The adjective for something put at risk, as in an endangered species.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受到威胁的、濒危的」

entries.definition: To make strong, built with the same -en ending but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 加强；与本词同为 -en 动词，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: To be a threat to someone, often of a person or mood.
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；对……构成危险（正式）

entries.definition: To frighten someone into doing what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓；胁迫（使人因害怕而服从）

entries.definition: To put someone or something in danger, with no suggestion of words.
entries.definitionCN: 危及（不含言语威胁之意）

entries.definition: To tell someone about a possible danger so they can avoid it.
entries.definitionCN: 警告（出于提醒，而非施压）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the -en verb pattern, the two main uses, and the passive form.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自 -en 动词规律、两种主要用法，以及被动式。

normal.en: Threaten is threat plus -en, the same way strength becomes strengthen.
normal.cn: threaten 就是 threat 加 -en，正如 strength 变成 strengthen。

normal.en: People threaten and things threaten: one with words, the other with pressure.
normal.cn: 人会威胁，物也会威胁：一个用言语，一个用压力。

normal.en: Threaten to rain is the sky making a promise it may not keep.
normal.cn: threaten to rain 是天空许下的一个未必兑现的承诺。

normal.en: Be threatened with closure means a job or a place is on the line.
normal.cn: be threatened with closure 意为一份工作或一个地方岌岌可危。

normal.en: The noun is threat; remember the verb carries the extra -en.
normal.cn: 名词是 threat；记住动词多带了 -en。

abstract.en: Picture a storm front pushing across the sky, pressing the whole town down before a drop falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一道雨锋推过天空，一滴雨未落就把整座城压住。

abstract.en: To threaten is to lean forward without stepping.
abstract.cn: threaten 是身体前倾，却不迈出那一步。

abstract.en: The verb gives danger a voice and a body: words at the door, water at the wall.
abstract.cn: 这个动词给危险一副嗓音和一具身体：门口的话语，墙外的水。

examples.en: The two firms threatened each other with lawsuits.
examples.cn: 两家公司互相威胁要打官司。

examples.en: Rising seas threaten these coastal farms.
examples.cn: 海面上升危及这些沿海农场。

examples.en: It threatened to snow all morning but never did.
examples.cn: 整个上午都像要下雪，却始终没下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死瑞腾」——死命拽着不放，逼得人腾不出身 → threaten 威胁

root: 名词 threat（日耳曼词根「压、挤」）加动词后缀 -en 构成，与 widen、strengthen 同型；由「出声施压」扩展为「以事物之势危及」，并衍生被动式「面临……威胁」。

sensesIntro.en: Threaten applies pressure in three voices: a person speaking harm, a force putting something at risk, and a sky that hints at what is coming.
sensesIntro.cn: threaten 以三种嗓音施加压力：人说出伤害、力量使某物处于险境、天空暗示即将来临之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storm front pressing across the sky before a single drop falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴雨未落就压过天空的雨锋。

branches.en: The voice: harm named out loud as leverage.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：把伤害说出口当作筹码。

branches.en: The force: smoke, water or heat doing the pressing.
branches.cn: 力量线：烟、水或热在施压。

branches.en: The sky: clouds that hint and never quite deliver.
branches.cn: 天空线：乌云暗示着，却往往落空。

branches.en: The institution: a library or a custom on the line.
branches.cn: 机构线：图书馆或习俗岌岌可危。

branches.en: Passive forms let anything be threatened, from health to a species.
branches.cn: 被动式让任何对象都能被威胁，从健康到物种。

intro.en: Threaten is a noun turned verb by -en, and the family adds -ing, -ed and -ly.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词加 -en 转成的动词，词族再叠加 -ing、-ed 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix are native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 抓住；攫取；抢占（机会）
definition_en: to take hold of something suddenly, or to take an opportunity quickly
core_image: 一只手猛地伸出，在栏杆滑落前牢牢握住它
scene: 他一把抓住栏杆。 He grabbed the railing.
sceneCN: 这里 grab 是「抓住」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他一把抓住栏杆。

derivatives.zh: 抓取器；抢夺者
贪心的；爱抢的

senses.title: To seize suddenly
senses.definition: to take hold of something quickly and roughly
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而粗暴地握住某物
senses.example: He grabbed the railing.
senses.exampleCN: 他一把抓住栏杆。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense of a sudden grasp.
senses.whyCN: 这是突然抓握的基本物理含义。

senses.title: To take a chance
senses.definition: to take an opportunity quickly before it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 在机会失去之前迅速把握
senses.example: She grabbed the chance to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住了出国留学的机会。
senses.why: An opportunity is treated like an object that can slip away.
senses.whyCN: 机会被当作可能滑走的物体来对待。

senses.title: A quick snatch
senses.definition: a sudden act of taking hold of something
senses.definitionCN: 突然握住某物的动作
senses.example: He made a grab for the falling cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸手去抓掉落的杯子。
senses.why: The noun keeps the suddenness of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了动词的突然性。

intro.en: Grab came into English from Low German and Dutch words for seizing.
intro.cn: grab 从低地德语和荷兰语中表示抓取的词进入英语。

items.en: Grabben meant to seize or snatch.
items.cn: grabben 意为抓住或抢夺。

items.en: Grabben carried the same grasping sense.
items.cn: grabben 带有同样的抓握含义。

items.en: Grab entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: grab 于十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: It spread from hands to chances and attention.
items.cn: 它从手部动作扩展到机会和注意力。

items.en: Up for grabs meant open to anyone.
items.cn: up for grabs 表示任何人都可以争取。

note.en: Grab is compared with look-alike words and verbs of seizing.
note.cn: 把 grab 与形近词以及表示抓取的动词作比较。

entries.definition: food, informally
entries.definitionCN: 食物（口语）

entries.definition: to smile widely
entries.definitionCN: 咧嘴笑

entries.definition: a sea creature with claws
entries.definitionCN: 蟹

entries.definition: to take hold forcefully
entries.definitionCN: 抓住；夺取

entries.definition: to grab quickly
entries.definitionCN: 一把抓走

entries.definition: to hold tightly
entries.definitionCN: 紧握

normalIntro.en: Grab is the hand closing before the mind has time to think.
normalIntro.cn: grab 是脑子还没想，手已经合拢。

normal.en: He grabbed the railing.
normal.cn: 他一把抓住栏杆。

normal.en: She grabbed the chance to study abroad.
normal.cn: 她抓住了出国留学的机会。

normal.en: He made a grab for the falling cup.
normal.cn: 他伸手去抓掉落的杯子。

normal.en: Let's grab a bite before the film.
normal.cn: 看电影前我们随便吃点东西吧。

normal.en: The last ticket is up for grabs.
normal.cn: 最后一张票人人可争。

abstract.en: Chances pass at the speed of hands.
abstract.cn: 机会以双手的速度经过。

abstract.en: What is grabbed in haste is often dropped in haste.
abstract.cn: 仓促抓来的，往往仓促丢下。

abstract.en: Attention is the one thing no hand can hold.
abstract.cn: 注意力是双手唯一握不住的东西。

examples.en: He grabbed the railing.
examples.cn: 他一把抓住栏杆。

examples.en: She grabbed the chance to study abroad.

examples.en: He made a grab for the falling cup.
examples.cn: 他伸手去抓掉落的杯子。

dict_mnemonic.text: grab 表示「猛地抓住」，可指抓东西、抓住机会，也可作名词表示「抓取」；grab attention 是「吸引注意」，grab a bite 是「随便吃点」，up for grabs 是「人人可争」。

root: 来自低地德语和荷兰语 grabben（抓取），十六世纪进入英语，核心义为迅速而有力地握住，后扩展到抓住机会、吸引注意等抽象用法。

sensesIntro.en: Grab means to seize something suddenly, to take an opportunity, or a quick act of seizing.
sensesIntro.cn: grab 指突然抓住某物、把握机会，或突然抓取的动作。

core.en: A hand closing fast on a thing.
core.cn: 迅速合拢在事物上的手。

branches.en: Fingers lock around a sliding rail.
branches.cn: 手指扣住正在滑落的栏杆。

branches.en: A door opens for a second and is taken.
branches.cn: 一扇门开了一瞬，随即被把握。

branches.en: A cup falls and a hand darts out.
branches.cn: 杯子落下，一只手猛地伸出。

branches.en: The verb and the noun both live in one instant.
branches.cn: 动词与名词都活在同一瞬间。

branches.en: A rail and a chance are both caught before they slip.
branches.cn: 栏杆与机会，都要在滑走前抓住。

intro.en: Grab forms agents, adjectives, and informal compounds.
intro.cn: grab 构成施事名词、形容词和口语复合词。

latinIntro.en: Grab is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: grab 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: He was grabbing at the rope.

items.meaning: a device or person that grabs
items.example: The robot has a metal grabber.
items.exampleCN: 机器人有一个金属抓取器。

items.example: The child was grabby with toys.

items.exampleCN: 这家店卖即取即走的餐食。

definition_zh: 受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者；（事故、疾病的）受害者
definition_en: a person harmed, injured or killed as the result of a crime, accident or other event
core_image: 一队被牵去献祭的牲畜，脖子上系着彩带，走在前头
scene: 火灾过后，邻居们围在被烧黑的门口，不知道该说什么。 The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
sceneCN: 这里 victim 是「受害者」（第 1 个义项：在灾难或罪案中受到伤害的人）；句意为洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。被牵去献祭的牲畜，就是这个词最早的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者

collocations.zh: 装可怜、摆出受害者姿态

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词加 -ize 构成
名词，义为「受害、迫害」
形容词，义为「无受害者的」，如 victimless crime
名词，义为「受害者身份」

senses.title: One harmed by another
senses.titleCN: 受害者：被罪案或他人伤害的人
senses.definition: a person harmed by a crime or by someone else’s action
senses.definitionCN: 被犯罪或他人行为伤害的人
senses.example: The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。
senses.why: Latin victima was the animal led to sacrifice; the modern sense keeps the picture of someone taken and harmed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victima 是被牵去献祭的牲畜；现代含义仍保留「被夺去并受伤害」的画面。

senses.title: One killed or injured
senses.titleCN: 遇难者：在事故或灾害中伤亡的人
senses.definition: a person killed or injured in an accident or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或灾害中死亡或受伤的人
senses.example: Road victims have fallen since the speed limit changed.
senses.exampleCN: 限速改变后，道路事故的死伤者减少了。
senses.why: No agent is needed here; the harm comes from events, not from a criminal.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要施害者：伤害来自事件，而不是罪犯。

senses.title: One suffering from illness
senses.definition: a person suffering from a disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 受某种疾病或状况折磨的人
senses.example: Many victims of the disease do not know they have it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多患这种病的人并不知道自己有。
senses.why: Illness is treated as an outer force that takes prisoners, much like an accident.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被当成一种抓走人的外部力量，与事故相似。

senses.title: A sacrifice
senses.titleCN: 牺牲品：为了别的目的而被舍弃的人或物
senses.definition: someone or something given up for another purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为别的目的被舍弃的人或物
senses.example: The old building became a victim of the redevelopment plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老建筑成了重建计划的牺牲品。
senses.why: Buildings cannot feel pain, yet the pattern holds: something old is given up for something new.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不会感到疼痛，但模式仍在：旧的东西为新的东西被舍弃了。

senses.title: A self-chosen role
senses.titleCN: 装出的受害者：把自己当成被亏待的人
senses.definition: a role taken on by someone who claims unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 某人自称受到不公而摆出的姿态
senses.example: He always plays the victim when the plan goes wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一出错，他就摆出受害者的姿态。
senses.why: The word turns ironic here: the person chooses the role instead of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词带了反讽：角色是自己选的，而不是被强加的。

intro.en: Victim comes from Latin victima, a beast offered in sacrifice, and has kept the sense of being taken and harmed.
intro.cn: victim 来自拉丁语 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，一直保留着「被夺去并受伤害」的意思。

items.en: Victima named the animal led to the altar, chosen and given up.
items.cn: victima 指被牵上祭坛的牲畜，被选中并被舍弃。

items.en: The word belonged to the language of sacrifice, with its sense of a life taken.
items.cn: 这个词属于献祭的语言，含「夺走一条生命」的意思。

items.en: French kept victime for a creature sacrificed or killed, sacred or not.
items.cn: 法语保留 victime，指被献祭或被杀的生命，不论是否神圣。

items.en: English took victim in the fifteenth century, widening it to anyone who suffers harm.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 victim，扩展到任何受到伤害的人。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to crime, disaster, disease and, ironically, to a chosen pose.
items.cn: 现代用法把它用于罪案、灾害、疾病，甚至反讽地指一种自愿摆出的姿态。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the victim- family; the near-meaning group holds words for those who suffer or are lost.
note.cn: 形近组沿 victim- 家族；近义组收表示受难者与损失的词。

entries.definition: To make someone a victim, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: The act of treating someone as a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害、被迫害」。

entries.definition: Having no harmed party, as in some crimes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无受害者的」。

entries.definition: The state of being a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害者身份」。

entries.definition: One who endures pain or illness, often long term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受苦者、患者」，多为长期。

entries.definition: One killed or wounded in fighting or an accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡者」，多用于战争与事故。

entries.definition: One who lived through the same event, the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幸存者」，同一事件的另一面。

entries.definition: The one aimed at, before any harm is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，伤害尚未发生前的一方。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the sacrifice picture and the phrase fall victim to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「献祭」的画面与 fall victim to 这一搭配。

normal.en: Victim once meant the animal led to the altar.
normal.cn: victim 原本指被牵上祭坛的牲畜。

normal.en: Fall victim to a scam means the trick caught you.
normal.cn: fall victim to a scam 指你被这个骗局抓住了。

normal.en: Victims of a flood are harmed by weather, not by a criminal.
normal.cn: 洪水的受害者是被天气所害，而不是被罪犯。

normal.en: Victimize is the verb: to make someone a victim.
normal.cn: victimize 是动词：使某人成为受害者。

normal.en: Playing the victim is a choice of role, not a fact.
normal.cn: playing the victim 是一种角色选择，不是事实。

abstract.en: The word began in sacrifice, and every later use keeps the shape of a life given up for something else.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于献祭，此后每种用法都保留着「为别的东西交出生命」的形状。

abstract.en: A victim is defined by what happened to them, which is why the word is passive in grammar and in feeling.
abstract.cn: 受害者是由遭遇定义的，所以这个词在语法和情感上都是被动的。

abstract.en: Naming someone a victim gives them sympathy but takes away agency, a tension the word never resolves.
abstract.cn: 称某人为受害者，给了他同情却拿走了主动性，这个矛盾这个词从未解决。

examples.en: The charity helps victims of domestic violence.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构帮助家庭暴力的受害者。

examples.en: Many small shops fell victim to the rise in rents.
examples.cn: 许多小店成了租金上涨的牺牲品。

examples.en: She was the victim of a cruel joke.
examples.cn: 她是一个恶作剧的受害者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克提姆」——维克（围）克（制）提（他）姆（母亲）受害了：受害者

root: 源自拉丁语名词 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，经法语 victime 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 victimize、victimization、victimhood。

sensesIntro.en: Victim stretches from the sacrificed animal to crime, accidents, illness, lost buildings and a chosen pose.
sensesIntro.cn: victim 从被献祭的牲畜，延伸到罪案、事故、疾病、被拆的建筑与自愿摆出的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal led to the altar with ribbons on its neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头脖子系着彩带、被牵向祭坛的牲畜。

branches.en: CRIME LINE: harmed by another person.
branches.cn: 罪案线：被他人所害。

branches.en: DISASTER LINE: injured by events.
branches.cn: 灾害线：被事件所伤。

branches.en: ILLNESS LINE: struck by disease.
branches.cn: 疾病线：被病痛击中。

branches.en: FIGURE LINE: a building given up, a role worn on purpose.
branches.cn: 比喻线：被舍弃的建筑，故意披上的角色。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a victim receives harm, a target is only aimed at.
branches.cn: 对照线：受害者已受到伤害，目标只是被瞄准。

intro.en: Victim is a complete Latin noun; English relatives add -ize, -ization, -hood and -less.
intro.cn: victim 是完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词加 -ize、-ization、-hood、-less。

latinIntro.en: The single Latin form is victima, a ritual word without a clear further root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式只有一个 victima，是礼仪用语，更早的词根并不明确。

definition_zh: 占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的
definition_en: having the greatest power or influence, describing a gene that shows its effect, or standing out most clearly
core_image: 长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都顺着它的方向说话
scene: 会议室里所有人都看向长桌顶端那个人。 One company has become dominant in the local taxi market.
sceneCN: 这里 dominant 是「占主导地位的」（第 1 个义项：在某个范围内拥有最大的权力或影响）；句意是有一家公司在本地出租车市场占了主导地位。

pos.zh: 形容词：占主导地位的；显性的；最突出的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「占主导地；显性地」
由前缀 pre-「在前」加本词构成，义为「占优势的；主要的」
由前缀 pre- 加同一词根构成，义为「占优势；占多数」

senses.title: Holding the most power
senses.definition: having the greatest power, influence or share within a group, market or place
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、市场或地方拥有最大的权力、影响或份额
senses.example: Two firms dominate the market, and both are dominant in pricing.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司主导着市场，二者在定价上都占主导地位。
senses.why: Latin dominus was the master of a household, and dominans described the one who masters; dominant is the state of being that master in a group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dominus 是一家之主，dominans 描述「正在当家」的人；dominant 就是一个群体里处于这种「主人」状态。

senses.title: Expressed in genetics
senses.definition: describes a gene or trait that appears in the offspring even when only one copy is inherited
senses.definitionCN: 描述只需继承一份就能在后代身上表现出来的基因或性状
senses.example: Brown eyes are dominant over blue eyes in this family.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个家族里，棕眼对蓝眼是显性的。
senses.why: The stronger gene behaves like the master of the household: as long as it is present, its effect is what the body shows.
senses.whyCN: 较强的基因像一家之主：只要它在场，身体表现出来的就是它的效果。

senses.title: Most noticeable
senses.definition: standing out most clearly in a view, a design or a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 在景色、设计或音乐中最清晰地显露出来的
senses.example: The dominant colour of the room is a deep green.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的主色调是深绿色。
senses.why: What stands highest or appears most often catches the eye first, so it takes over the scene as a master takes over a room.
senses.whyCN: 最高的东西或出现最多的东西最先抓住目光，于是它像主人占据屋子一样占据了整个画面。

intro.en: Dominant is the present participle of Latin dominari, to rule, from dominus, master of a household.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根是 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Domus meant house or household, and it also gave dominus, the master of the house.
items.cn: domus 指房子或家户，并生出 dominus（一家之主）。

items.en: Dominari meant to rule or to have mastery over others.
items.cn: dominari 意为「统治、支配他人」。

items.en: The present participle dominans described someone or something that is ruling at that moment.
items.cn: 现在分词 dominans 描述此刻正在起支配作用的人或物。

items.en: Old French dominant carried the adjective into English usage.
items.cn: 古法语 dominant 把这个形容词带入英语用法。

items.en: English used it for political and social power before science borrowed it for genes.
items.cn: 英语先把它用于政治与社会权力，后来科学才借去指基因。

items.en: The word now also names the most visible colour, note or feature.
items.cn: 今天这个词也用来指最显眼的颜色、音符或特征。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the Latin dominus root; the near-meaning group gathers words for power and prominence.
note.cn: 形近组守着拉丁语 dominus 词根；近义组收的是表示权力与突出地位的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to rule, control or be the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「支配、控制、占首要地位」，与 dominant 同根。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being dominant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势、支配地位」，指处于 dominant 的状态。

entries.definition: Most common or most noticeable; formed with the prefix pre-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占优势的、主要的」，由前缀 pre- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: Most important or most successful at a particular time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「领先的、最重要的」，强调位置靠前。

entries.definition: Having the power to direct or restrain others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「控制性的、起支配作用的」，强调施加约束。

entries.definition: The largest or most important of several things; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「主要的」，在若干事物中最大或最重要，语气更平实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real dominus family and the places dominance actually shows.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着真实的 dominus 词族，以及支配地位真正显现的场合。

normal.en: Dominus is the master of a house; dominant is the one acting as master.
normal.cn: dominus 是一家之主，dominant 就是正在当家的那一个。

normal.en: Dominari means to rule, so dominant describes whoever rules the group.
normal.cn: dominari 意为统治，dominant 描述统治这个群体的那一方。

normal.en: A dominant gene speaks loudest even when it is alone.
normal.cn: 显性基因即使只有一份，声音也最响。

normal.en: A dominant colour is the one the eye notices before all others.
normal.cn: 主色调就是眼睛先于其他颜色注意到的那个颜色。

normal.en: Pre- plus dominant gives predominant, a near twin meaning most common.
normal.cn: pre- 加 dominant 得到 predominant，意思接近「最常见、最占优势」。

abstract.en: Picture one chair at the end of a long table, slightly taller than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌尽头有一把椅子，比其余的都略高一点。

abstract.en: Picture one green wall making every other colour in the room look pale.
abstract.cn: 想象一面绿墙让屋里其他颜色都显得淡了。

abstract.en: Picture a single voice that everyone else unconsciously follows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音，其他所有人都不自觉地跟着它走。

examples.en: English is the dominant language in international business.
examples.cn: 英语是国际商务中的主导语言。

examples.en: The dominant feature of the valley is a long ridge.
examples.cn: 这个山谷最突出的特征是那道长长的山脊。

examples.en: In this species, dark feathers are dominant over pale ones.
examples.cn: 在这个物种里，深色羽毛对浅色羽毛是显性的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多密难」——人一多、关系一密，就难分高下；最后站上风的那个就是 dominant。

root: 源自拉丁语 dominans，是 dominari（统治）的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主），再往前是 domus（房子、家户）。因此 dominant 本义是「像主人一样当家、压过别人」，后扩展指显性基因与最突出的特征。

sensesIntro.en: From a master of a household to a ruling firm, a loud gene and the colour that takes over a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一家之主，到主导市场的公司，再到声音最响的基因和占满屋子的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair at the head of the table that everyone turns toward.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌尽头那把椅子，所有人都朝向它。

branches.en: POWER: the first sense is the social and economic mastery of a group or market.
branches.cn: 权力线：第一个义项是群体或市场中的社会与经济支配力。

branches.en: HEREDITY: the same mastery appears in a gene that overrides its partner.
branches.cn: 遗传线：同样的支配力出现在压过配对基因的显性基因上。

branches.en: ATTENTION: whatever stands out most takes over the eye's field.
branches.cn: 注意线：最突出的东西占据视野。

branches.en: Power and visibility overlap: the strongest feature is usually the one seen first.
branches.cn: 权力与可见度重叠：最强的特征通常也是最先被看见的。

branches.en: Social dominance and genetic dominance share the image of a master that cannot be ignored.
branches.cn: 社会支配与基因显性共享同一幅画面：一个无法被忽视的主人。

intro.en: Dominant is a Latin present participle in -ans, built on dominus, master of a house.
intro.cn: dominant 是拉丁语以 -ans 结尾的现在分词，其根为 dominus（一家之主）。

latinIntro.en: Latin domus, dominus and dominari are recorded; the title dominus also survives in church language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domus、dominus 与 dominari 均有记录；dominus 这一称呼也保留在教会用语中。

items.example: The household is the base of the image.
items.exampleCN: 家户是这幅画面的基底。

items.example: The master sits at the head of the table.
items.exampleCN: 一家之主坐在长桌尽头。

items.example: The verb names the act of ruling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指统治的动作。

items.example: It became the English adjective dominant.
items.exampleCN: 它变成了英语形容词 dominant。

items.example: It forms dominant from the participle.
items.exampleCN: 它把分词变成 dominant 这一形容词。

items.example: The firm holds dominance in the region.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在该地区占支配地位。
一支队伍控制了整场比赛。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「优势；支配地位」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「占主导地；显性地」
由前缀 pre-「在前」加本词构成，义为「占优势的；主要的」

definition_zh: 城市的；都市的；城镇的；具有城市特点的
definition_en: relating to a town or city and to life in it
core_image: 傍晚一片连成线的窗灯
scene: 公交车在高架桥上慢慢挪动，两边楼群一路亮到天边。 Air quality in urban areas is a constant concern.
sceneCN: 这里 urban 是「城市的」（第 1 个义项：与城市有关的）；句意为城区的空气质量一直是令人担心的事。连成线的窗灯，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 urban 加 -ization 构成名词，义为「城市化」
由 urban 加 -ize 构成动词，义为「使城市化」
同源但语义分化，义为「文雅的；有都市风度的」
同源名词，义为「郊区」，sub- 表示「靠近、在下」

senses.title: Belonging to a town or city
senses.definition: connected with a town or city rather than the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 与城镇或城市相关，而非乡村
senses.example: Urban areas grew quickly in the last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年城区扩展得很快。
senses.why: The adjective comes from the Latin word for city, so its first job is simply to mark what belongs to a city.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词源自拉丁语「城」一词，因此首要功能就是标出「属于城市的」。

senses.title: Characteristic of city living
senses.definition: used of habits, problems, or styles typical of city life
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市生活特有的习惯、问题或风格
senses.example: Noise and crowding are urban problems.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音和拥挤是城市的问题。
senses.why: Once a district exists, the habits that grow in it carry the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 城区一旦形成，在其中长出来的习惯也就带着同一个形容词。

senses.title: Relating to city government or services
senses.definition: used of the services and authorities of a city
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市的公共服务与市政机构
senses.example: Urban water supply was restored on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 城区供水星期一恢复了。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to a city, and the city's own offices belong to it most directly.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出属于城市的事物，而市政府本身最直接地属于它。

senses.title: Designed for dense settlement
senses.definition: used of land used for buildings and roads rather than farming
senses.definitionCN: 形容用于建筑与道路而非耕作的土地
senses.example: Urban land costs far more than farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 城市用地比农田贵得多。
senses.why: The same city picture works on the ground itself: land inside the city is marked out for buildings.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅城市图景落在土地上：城里的地标出来是给房子用的。

senses.title: Polished in manner, in one old sense
senses.definition: an older sense describing refined manners, now kept in the word urbane
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指举止风雅，如今主要见于 urbane 一词
senses.example: His manners were urban in the older sense of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 按这个词的旧义，他的举止相当文雅。
senses.why: City life was once thought to polish people, so the adjective briefly praised good manners as well.
senses.whyCN: 人们一度认为城市生活能使人变得文雅，因此这个形容词也曾用来称赞好举止。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of the city, borrowed straight into English in its original shape.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语的「城市」形容词，几乎以原形直接借入英语。

items.en: Urbs meant a city, and urbanus meant of a city or belonging to city life.
items.cn: urbs 意为「城市」，urbanus 意为「城市的、都市生活的」。

items.en: Urbanus also came to describe manners thought polished in the city.
items.cn: urbanus 也渐渐用来形容在城里养成的风雅举止。

items.en: The adjective passed through French as urbain before reaching English.
items.cn: 这个形容词经由法语 urbain 再进入英语。

items.en: Urban enters English in the seventeenth century as a plain adjective of the city.
items.cn: urban 于十七世纪进入英语，是朴素的「城市的」形容词。

items.en: Its relatives multiply: urbane for manners, urbanization for a process.
items.cn: 同源词此后增多：urbane 指风度，urbanization 指过程。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin city root, while the near-meaning group compares terms of settlement and land.
note.cn: 形近组汇集建在拉丁「城」词根上的词，近义组比较聚落与土地类词。

entries.definition: polished in manner
entries.definitionCN: 文雅的；有礼的

entries.definition: the area around a city
entries.definitionCN: 郊区

entries.definition: the growth of city life
entries.definitionCN: 城市化

entries.definition: to make into a city
entries.definitionCN: 使城市化

entries.definition: relating to a town's government
entries.definitionCN: 市政的

entries.definition: relating to a large city
entries.definitionCN: 大都市的

entries.definition: relating to citizens and a city
entries.definitionCN: 市民的；公民的

entries.definition: relating to the countryside
entries.definitionCN: 乡村的

normalIntro.en: One Latin root for the city, shared with suburb and urbane.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语「城」的词根，与 suburb、urbane 同出。

normal.en: Urb- means city: urban, suburb, urbane all contain it.
normal.cn: urb- 意为「城」：urban、suburb、urbane 都含着它。

normal.en: Urban planning and urban areas are the fixed phrases.
normal.cn: urban planning 与 urban areas 是固定搭配。

normal.en: The opposite is rural, not suburban.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 rural，不是 suburban。

normal.en: Urbane looks similar but means polished in manner.
normal.cn: urbane 长得像，意思是「文雅的」。

normal.en: Urbanization names the process, urbanize the verb.
normal.cn: urbanization 指过程，urbanize 是动词。

abstract.en: See a line of windows lit up to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一排窗灯一直亮到天边。

abstract.en: Hear buses and voices under a bridge at night.
abstract.cn: 夜里听桥下的车声与人声。

abstract.en: Look down from a high building at streets in a grid.
abstract.cn: 从高楼俯瞰方格状的街道。

examples.en: Urban life can be exciting but also tiring.
examples.cn: 城市生活令人兴奋，也让人疲惫。

examples.en: The council is reviewing its urban planning rules.
examples.cn: 市议会正在复核城市规划条例。

examples.en: More than half the population now lives in urban areas.
examples.cn: 现在有一半以上的人口住在城区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿本」——到了城里先想的是找个地方填饱肚子，这座城对饿着的人来说就是城市本身。

root: 拉丁语 urbanus（城市的），源自 urbs（城市），经法语 urbain 进入英语；urbs 本指有城墙的城

sensesIntro.en: One root marked the walled city; it now marks districts, problems, services, land use, and once-polished manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个原本标出城墙之城的词根，如今标出城区、城市问题、市政、用地与旧日的风雅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of lit windows running to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一路亮到天边的窗灯。

branches.en: The district branch: the built-up area itself.
branches.cn: 区域分支：建成区本身。

branches.en: The life branch: noise, crowding, speed.
branches.cn: 生活分支：噪音、拥挤与速度。

branches.en: The government branch: city halls and their work.
branches.cn: 市政分支：市政府及其事务。

branches.en: The land branch: plots given to buildings.
branches.cn: 土地分支：划给建筑的地块。

branches.en: The manner branch: the old city ideal of polish.
branches.cn: 风度分支：旧时城里人推崇的风雅。

intro.en: A Latin adjective ending on a root that also gives suburb and urbane.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁形容词词尾压在同时也派生出 suburb 与 urbane 的词根上。

latinIntro.en: Latin urbs, city, with urbicarius for what belongs to a city, and urbanitas for city refinement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 urbs 指城，urbicarius 指属于城市的，urbanitas 指都市的风雅。

items.example: Suburb means the area near a city.

definition_zh: 存在；生存；生活方式
definition_en: the state of being real or present; a way of living; being itself
core_image: 某样东西被证实真实地在那里
scene: 没有人能证明那种神秘生物的存在。 No one can prove the existence of that mysterious creature.
sceneCN: 这里 existence 是「存在」（第 1 个义项）；句意：没有人能证明那种神秘生物的存在。

derivatives.zh: 存在的；现存的
存在主义的；关于存在的
存在主义
共存；共处

senses.title: State of being real
senses.definition: the state of being real or present
senses.definitionCN: 真实或有事物存在的状态
senses.example: The existence of dark matter is widely accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 暗物质的存在已被广泛接受。
senses.why: The noun names the fact of being real.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指「真实存在」这一事实。

senses.title: Way of living
senses.definition: a way of living, often a hard or simple one
senses.definitionCN: 一种生活状态，常指艰苦或简朴的生活
senses.example: The farmer led a simple existence.
senses.exampleCN: 那位农夫过着简朴的生活。
senses.why: Being real becomes the shape of a daily life.
senses.whyCN: 「存在」具体化为日常生活的样子。

senses.title: Being itself
senses.definition: being itself, as studied in philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 哲学所研究的存在本身
senses.example: The book asks what existence really means.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书追问存在究竟意味着什么。
senses.why: The everyday fact is raised to an abstract idea.
senses.whyCN: 日常事实被提升为抽象概念。

intro.en: Existence comes from Latin exsistentia, the noun of exsistere.
intro.cn: existence 源自拉丁语 exsistentia，是 exsistere 的名词形式。

items.en: Exsistere means to come forth and appear.
items.cn: exsistere 意为出现并显现。

items.en: Exsistentia names the resulting state.
items.cn: exsistentia 指由此形成的状态。

items.en: Existence keeps the sense of being present.
items.cn: existence 保留「在场存在」的含义。

items.en: Existence enters as a learned word.
items.cn: existence 作为学术用词进入英语。

items.en: Existence spreads from philosophy to daily use.
items.cn: existence 从哲学扩展到日常用语。

items.en: A simple existence now describes a way of life.
items.cn: a simple existence 如今可描述一种生活方式。

note.en: Existence is about being; insistence is about demanding.
note.cn: existence 关乎存在，insistence 则关乎坚持。

entries.definition: the act of demanding firmly

entries.definition: the state of having just enough to live

entries.definition: continuing despite difficulty

normalIntro.en: Existence is the noun for the fact of being.
normalIntro.cn: existence 是表示「存在」这一事实的名词。

normal.en: The existence of the tribe was never doubted.
normal.cn: 这个部落的存在从未被怀疑。

normal.en: He survived on a bare existence in the hills.
normal.cn: 他在山里过着勉强糊口的生活。

normal.en: Philosophers still argue about existence.
normal.cn: 哲学家至今仍在争论存在的问题。

normal.en: The charity brought the school into existence.
normal.cn: 这家慈善机构促成了这所学校的建立。

normal.en: Few species can maintain existence in that heat.
normal.cn: 很少有物种能在那种高温中维持生存。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint that proves someone was there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脚印证明有人来过。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin thread holding a heavy weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线吊着重物。

abstract.en: Think of a single star in an empty sky.
abstract.cn: 想象空旷夜空中唯一的一颗星。

examples.en: The existence of the document changed the case.
examples.cn: 这份文件的存在改变了案件走向。

examples.en: She described her existence as quiet and simple.
examples.cn: 她把自己的生活形容为安静而简朴。

examples.en: Ancient thinkers asked what existence itself is.
examples.cn: 古代思想家追问存在本身是什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「existence」中有 exist（存在），后面接 -ence 变成名词：存在的状态就是「存在」。

branches.en: That fact becomes the shape of a life.

branches.cn: 这一事实被提升为哲学概念。

branches.en: Both concern real presence in the world.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及在世界中的真实在场。

branches.en: The concrete fact and the abstract idea pair up.
branches.cn: 具体事实与抽象概念相互对应。

intro.cn: existence 在 exist 之后加上名词后缀 -ence。

latinIntro.en: Latin exsistere and exsistentia supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exsistere 与 exsistentia 提供核心词形。

Exist is the verb base of existence.

senses.definition: an alcoholic drink made from grain

senses.example: They shared a cold beer after work.

senses.title: A glass or serving of beer

abstract.en: See beads of water on a cold glass.
abstract.cn: 想象冰杯壁上挂着水珠。

abstract.en: See white foam rising in a glass.

abstract.en: See friends at a small table on a summer night.

definition_zh: 评估；评定；估算；核定（税额）
definition_en: to judge or estimate the value, quality, or amount of something, to rate a person's work, or to fix a tax
core_image: 一只手把砝码放上天平，看两边是否平衡
scene: 查勘员蹲在开裂的墙边，用卷尺量着裂缝的长度。 The engineer assessed the damage after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 assess 是「评估、估算」（第 1 个义项：判断损失、价值或风险的大小）；句意为「洪水过后，工程师评估了损失」。画面中有开裂的墙、卷尺与蹲在墙边的查勘员。

pos.zh: 动词：评估；评定；估算；核定（税额）

derivatives.zh: 由 assess 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「评估；评定；核定」
由 assess 加 -or 构成，义为「评估员；估税员」
由 assess 加 -able 构成，义为「可评估的；可征税的」
由前缀 re- 加 assess 构成，义为「重新评估」

senses.title: To judge the value or size
senses.definition: to judge or estimate the value, size, risk, or seriousness of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断或估算某物的价值、规模、风险或严重程度
senses.example: The engineer assessed the damage after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，工程师评估了损失。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to sit beside, and an assessor sat beside a judge to weigh a case.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「坐在旁边」，估税员正是坐在法官旁边，为案子称一称分量。

senses.title: To rate a person's work
senses.definition: to judge the quality of a student's work or a person's ability, often formally
senses.definitionCN: 评定学生作业或某人能力的水平，常为正式评定
senses.example: Teachers assess each essay against the same standards.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们按同一套标准评定每篇作文。
senses.why: Weighing an object and weighing a pupil's work use the same gesture: set it against a standard.
senses.whyCN: 称一件物品与评一份作业用的是同一个动作：把它放到标准旁边。

senses.title: To fix a tax or charge
senses.definition: to calculate and fix the amount of tax, fine, or payment owed by someone
senses.definitionCN: 计算并确定某人应缴的税额、罚款或费用
senses.example: The council assessed the property at a higher rate.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会按更高的税率核定了这处房产的税额。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded use: an official sits beside the property and fixes what it owes.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的用法：官员坐在产业旁边，定下它该缴多少。

intro.en: Assess begins with a Latin image of someone sitting beside another to weigh a matter.
intro.cn: assess 起初是一个拉丁意象：有人坐在另一个人旁边，为事情称一称分量。

items.en: The root 「*sed-」 meant 'to sit', and it lies behind many Latin words for sitting and settling.
items.cn: 词根「*sed-」意为「坐」，拉丁语中许多表示坐与安顿的词都由它而来。

items.en: Assidere meant 'to sit beside', from ad- 'to' plus sedere 'to sit'.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sedere「坐」构成。

items.en: An assessor was an official who sat beside a magistrate to fix taxes and fines.
items.cn: assessor 是坐在长官旁边、协助核定税额与罚金的官员。

items.en: Assesser took the verb form and kept the sense of fixing an amount owed.
items.cn: 古法语 assesser 取下动词形式，保留「核定应缴数额」的意思。

items.en: English assess began with taxes and fines, and only later widened to judging value in general.
items.cn: 英语里的 assess 先用于税额与罚金，后来才放宽到泛指评估价值。

items.en: Now pupils, risks, damage and property can all be assessed, with the same weighing gesture.
items.cn: 如今学生、风险、损失与房产都可以被 assess，用的是同一个称量的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs close to assess in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of judging and estimating.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与 assess 接近的动词；近义组收表示判断与估算的动词。

entries.definition: To own or have something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥有、具有」。

entries.definition: The right or chance to use or reach something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「使用权、接近的机会」。

entries.definition: To help someone do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「帮助、协助」。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something carefully.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细判断某物的价值或质量。

entries.definition: To calculate an approximate value or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 计算出一个大约的价值或数量。

entries.definition: To form an opinion about something after thought.
entries.definitionCN: 经过思考后对某事形成看法。

entries.definition: To give something a particular level of quality or value.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物定出某种质量或价值等级。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from weights on a scale to a marked essay, a tax bill and a measured risk.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从天平上的砝码，走到批改的作文、税单与衡量的风险。

normal.en: Assess: put the object beside the standard and weigh it.
normal.cn: assess：把对象放到标准旁边，称一称。

normal.en: An assessor sits beside the judge.
normal.cn: 估税员坐在法官旁边。

normal.en: Assess an essay: the work is placed against a mark scheme.

normal.en: Assess a tax: the property is weighed for what it owes.
normal.cn: 核定税额：把产业称一称，看它该缴多少。

normal.en: Assess a risk: the danger is put on the same scale.

abstract.en: Everything assessed is weighed against something else.
abstract.cn: 凡被 assess 的东西，都是被放到另一样东西旁边称量。

abstract.en: Tax, teaching and risk all use the same gesture.
abstract.cn: 税务、教学与风险用的是同一个动作。

abstract.en: The word began at a judge's side and spread to every scale.
abstract.cn: 这个词从法官身旁开始，扩散到每一架天平。

examples.en: The engineer assessed the damage after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，工程师评估了损失。

examples.en: Teachers assess each essay against the same standards.
examples.cn: 老师们按同一套标准评定每篇作文。

examples.en: The council assessed the property at a higher rate.
examples.cn: 市政会按更高的税率核定了这处房产的税额。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿塞斯」——阿塞斯把砝码放上天平，估一估那堆东西的分量：评估

root: assess 来自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sedere「坐」构成；assessor 原是坐在长官旁边、协助核定税额与罚金的官员。因此它先表示「核定应缴数额」，后来放宽为「评估价值、损失、风险」，再延伸到「评定学生的表现」。三个义项的共同动作都是把对象放到某个标准旁边，称一称它的分量。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one gesture, weighing against a standard: judging value or risk, rating a pupil's work, and fixing a tax.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共享同一个动作，把对象放到标准旁边称量：判断价值或风险、评定学生作业，以及核定税额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand setting a weight on a balance to see whether the two sides match.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把砝码放上天平，看两边是否平衡。

branches.en: THE SCALE LINE: value, damage and risk are all weighed.
branches.cn: 天平线：价值、损失与风险都要过秤。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: a pupil's work is placed against a standard.
branches.cn: 学校线：学生的作业被放到标准旁边。

branches.en: THE TAX LINE: an official fixes what a property owes.
branches.cn: 税务线：官员定下产业该缴多少。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL LINE: the first assessors sat beside magistrates.
branches.cn: 公务线：最早的估税员坐在长官旁边。

branches.en: THE STANDARD LINE: every assessment needs something to compare against.
branches.cn: 标准线：任何评估都需要一个可比照的东西。

definition_zh: 互联网；因特网；网络接入与线上世界
definition_en: the worldwide system of interconnected computer networks that uses common protocols to carry data

scene: 深夜的书房里，学生戴上耳机，屏幕上来自另一座城市的课程视频几乎立刻加载完成。 The Internet carries the lecture across continents in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里指把全球计算机网络连成一体、承载数据传输的系统（第 1 个义项：全球互联网）；句意：互联网在几秒内把这堂课传过多个大洲。

pos.zh: 互联网；因特网；网络接入

senses.title: The worldwide network of networks
senses.definition: the global system that joins countless local and national networks through shared protocols
senses.definitionCN: 通过共同协议把无数地方性与国家级网络连成一体的全球系统
senses.example: The internet links universities on every continent.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网把各大洲的大学连接起来。
senses.why: The name says what it is: a net that sits between other nets and lets them reach one another.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字直说其本质：一张位于其他网络之间、让它们互通的网。

senses.title: A service you subscribe to
senses.definition: the connection to the global network that a household or business buys from a provider
senses.definitionCN: 家庭或企业向服务商购买、用于接入全球网络的连接服务
senses.example: The village finally got internet last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子去年冬天终于通上了网络。
senses.why: People meet the system through a paid link, so the mass noun also names the service rather than the whole architecture.
senses.whyCN: 人们是通过付费连接接触到这个系统的，因此这个不可数名词也指服务，而不只是整套架构。

senses.title: The online world people inhabit
senses.definition: the space of websites, messages and communities reached through the network
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络访问的网站、信息与社群所构成的空间
senses.example: She found the answer somewhere on the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上某处找到了答案。
senses.why: Once access is routine, the word shifts from the machinery to the place-like experience of being online.
senses.whyCN: 当接入成为日常，这个词便从机器设施转向「在网上」那种空间化的体验。

senses.title: Any interconnection of networks
senses.definition: the general technical condition in which separate networks are joined, often written without the capital
senses.definitionCN: 彼此独立的网络被连接起来的一般技术状态，常以小写形式书写
senses.example: Two research internet links now carry the telescope data.
senses.exampleCN: 两条研究网络互联链路现在承载着望远镜数据。
senses.why: Before it named one global system, the word was a plain description of interconnecting nets, and that technical sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 在它专指一个全球系统之前，这个词只是「网络互联」的普通描述，这一技术义至今仍在。

senses.title: The medium that carries content
senses.definition: the network understood as a channel through which media, trade and speech are delivered
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为传送媒体、交易与言论的通道的网络
senses.example: Radio survived by moving its audience to the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 广播通过把听众转移到互联网上而存活下来。
senses.why: A network that carries data can be described by what it carries, so the word also names a medium.
senses.whyCN: 承载数据的网络可以从「承载什么」来描述，因此这个词也指一种媒介。

senses.title: The link itself
senses.definition: the active connection between a device and the network, as in having or losing it
senses.definitionCN: 设备与网络之间正在生效的连接，如「有网」或「断网」
senses.example: My phone lost internet halfway through the call.
senses.exampleCN: 通话到一半时我的手机断了网。
senses.why: The whole system is only present to a user through a live link, so the word can name that link.
senses.whyCN: 对用户而言，整个系统只通过一条生效的链路显现，因此这个词可以指那条链路。

senses.title: The industry built around it
senses.definition: the businesses, platforms and jobs that depend on the network
senses.definitionCN: 依赖该网络运作的企业、平台与岗位
senses.example: Advertising moved most of its budget to the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 广告业把大部分预算转向了互联网。
senses.why: An infrastructure with its own economy is naturally named by the same word, as in internet companies.
senses.whyCN: 拥有自身经济形态的基础设施自然沿用同一个词来命名，如网络公司。

senses.title: The store of online material
senses.definition: the accumulated pages, records and data reachable through the network
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络可以访问的网页、记录与数据的累积总和
senses.example: The whole archive is now on the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 整个档案现在都放在了网上。
senses.why: If the network holds the material, speakers treat the medium as the store, giving this collective sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果网络承载着这些材料，说话人就会把媒介当作仓库，于是有了这一集合义。

intro.en: Internet is a twentieth-century compound of Latin inter, meaning between, and English net, a clipping of network; the capital letter once marked a single global system.
intro.cn: 这个词是二十世纪的复合词：拉丁语「在……之间」加英语「网络」的缩略；首字母大写曾用来标记那个唯一的全球系统。

items.en: Inter meant between or among, and it survives in many English words for things that sit between others.
items.cn: 这个词缀意为「在……之间」或「在……之中」，在许多表示「位于其间」的英语词中留存。

items.en: Net was already a short word for a network, especially a network of computers or communications.
items.cn: 「网」早已是网络的简短说法，尤其指计算机或通信网络。

items.en: The first packet-switching network linked a handful of research sites, and similar networks soon appeared in other countries.
items.cn: 第一个分组交换网络连接了几个研究站点，类似网络很快在其他国家出现。

items.en: The compound was formed to name the linking of separate networks, and it soon became the ordinary word for the global system.
items.cn: 人们造出这个复合词来指独立网络的互联，它很快成为指称全球系统的普通词。

items.en: Style guides long insisted on a capital letter for the single global system and a small letter for any interconnection of networks; everyday use now blurs the two.
items.cn: 旧式规范坚持：指唯一的全球系统时首字母大写，指任意网络互联时小写；日常使用如今已把两者混同。

items.en: The exact first use and the identity of the coiner are not settled; the date around 1972 is generally accepted, but earlier and independent formations have been claimed.
items.cn: 确切的首次使用与造词者尚无定论；约 1972 年这一年代为一般接受，但更早或独立造词的用法也有人主张。

note.en: The first group shares the net idea at different scales; the second group names the online world under other aspects.
note.cn: 第一组是不同尺度上的「网」；第二组从其他侧面指称线上世界。

entries.definition: A private network inside an organization, built with the same technology but closed to outsiders.
entries.definitionCN: 机构内部的专用网络，技术相同但对外封闭。

entries.definition: A private network opened to selected outside partners, sitting between an intranet and the public network.
entries.definitionCN: 向特定外部合作方开放的专用网络，介于内部网络与公共网络之间。

entries.definition: One linked system; the internet is the network that joins many such systems.
entries.definitionCN: 单个互联系统；而互联网是把许多这样的系统连起来的那张网。

entries.definition: To join networks to one another, the action behind the name.
entries.definitionCN: 把网络彼此连接，正是名称背后的动作。

entries.definition: The online world imagined as a place; it stresses experience and culture rather than cables.
entries.definitionCN: 把线上世界想象成一个场所；强调体验与文化，而非线缆。

entries.definition: The linked pages and services built on the network; it is one layer, not the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在该网络之上的网页与服务；它只是其中一层，不是整个系统。

entries.definition: Being connected and active on a network; it describes a state rather than naming the system.
entries.definitionCN: 已连接并在网络上活动；描述状态，而不是命名系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin and English pieces and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语与英语成分，以及真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Inter means between, so the internet is the net between nets.
normal.cn: 「之间」加上「网」，互联网就是网与网之间的那张网。

normal.en: The family runs internet, intranet, extranet, interconnect and internetwork.
normal.cn: 同族词包括互联网、内部网络、外部专用网络、互联与网际网络。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark access: internet access, internet connection, internet service.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出接入：互联网接入、网络连接、互联网服务。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark scale: internet traffic, internet user, internet address.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：网络流量、互联网用户、网络地址。

normal.en: The capital letter used to say that there is only one such global system.
normal.cn: 首字母大写过去用来表示这样的全球系统只有一个。

abstract.en: Picture a city where every street ends at a station that also leads to every other city.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，每条街的尽头都有一个通往其他所有城市的车站。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are in many buildings but share one catalogue.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架分散在许多建筑里，却共用一份目录。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation in which every sentence can reach every listener at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一场对话，每句话都能同时传到每一位听众那里。

examples.en: The internet was designed to keep working even when one route failed.
examples.cn: 互联网的设计目标是即使某条线路失效也能继续工作。

examples.en: Many rural clinics still lack reliable internet.
examples.cn: 许多乡村诊所仍然缺乏稳定的网络接入。

examples.en: He taught himself the language entirely on the internet.
examples.cn: 他完全靠在网上自学了这门语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特」近「之间」加「网」——网与网之间连成的那张网

root: 拉丁语「在……之间」加英语「网络」的缩略；约 1972 年组合成词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the global architecture to the service, the online world, the plain technical sense, the medium, the active link, the industry and the stored material.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从全球架构出发，依次落到服务、线上世界、纯技术义、媒介、生效链路、产业与所存资料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many separate networks joined so that any point can reach any other point.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多独立网络被连接起来，使任意一点都能到达另一点。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM ITSELF: the global network of networks, the sense that anchors all the others.
branches.cn: 系统本身：全球的网络之网，是支撑其余义项的锚点。

branches.en: THE LINK A USER HAS: a paid service or a live connection that stands between a device and the system.
branches.cn: 用户拥有的链路：付费服务或生效连接，位于设备与系统之间。

branches.en: THE PLACE IT FEELS LIKE: the online world of sites, messages and communities.
branches.cn: 它带来的场所感：网站、信息与社群构成的线上世界。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL READING: any joining of separate networks, written without the capital.
branches.cn: 技术读法：任意独立网络的互联，通常小写书写。

branches.en: WHAT IT CARRIES AND SUPPORTS: a medium for content, an industry around it, and a store of reachable material.
branches.cn: 它所承载与支撑的：内容媒介、围绕它的产业，以及可访问资料的总和。

intro.en: Internet is Latin inter plus English net; the prefix is productive, while the base is a native clipping.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语前缀「之间」加英语「网」的缩略构成；前缀能产，词基是英语本族缩略。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin element is the prefix inter; the base net is English, so Latin cognates are listed for the prefix alone.
latinIntro.cn: 唯一的拉丁成分是前缀「之间」；词基「网」来自英语，因此只为前缀列出拉丁同族。

items.example: The prefix places the network between other networks.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把这张网放在其他网络之间。

items.example: The base is the short English word for a network.
items.exampleCN: 词基是英语中「网络」的简短说法。

items.example: The compound names the joining of separate networks.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指独立网络的互联。

items.example: An intranet serves only the staff of one organization.
items.exampleCN: 内部网络只为一个机构的员工服务。

items.meaning: a network opened to selected outsiders
items.meaningCN: 对特定外部方开放的网络
items.example: An extranet lets partners see part of the system.
items.exampleCN: 外部专用网络让合作方看到系统的一部分。

items.example: Engineers interconnect the two campus networks.
items.exampleCN: 工程师把两个校园网连接起来。

items.meaningCN: 由多个网络互联而成的系统
items.example: The term describes the architecture in general.
items.exampleCN: 这个词泛指这种互联架构。

items.example: An internet-based service needs no local server.
items.exampleCN: 基于互联网的服务不需要本地服务器。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「内部」的拉丁前缀替换首段构成，义为「机构内部网络」
由表示「外部」的拉丁前缀替换首段构成，义为「对外部合作方开放的网络」
由表示「之间」的前缀加「连接」的动词构成，义为「使互联」
由该名词加表示「以……为基础」的词尾构成，义为「基于互联网的」

definition_zh: 远的；久远的；疏远的
definition_en: far away in space or time, or not friendly and not paying attention
core_image: 山顶的信号塔在雾里只剩一个模糊的小点
scene: 车开出很久，那座塔缩成雾里的一个小点。 He grew distant after the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 distant 指「疏远的」（第 3 个义项：不再亲近）；句意是争吵之后他变得疏远起来。

derivatives.zh: 距离
遥远地；冷淡地

senses.title: Far away in space
senses.definition: a long way from the place where you are
senses.definitionCN: 离你所在之处有很长一段路
senses.example: A distant hill turned blue in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨里远处的山变成了蓝色。
senses.why: The further a thing is, the fewer details it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 东西越远，留下的细节越少。

senses.title: Far back in time
senses.definition: happening a long time ago or a long time from now
senses.definitionCN: 发生在很久以前或很久以后
senses.example: Those are stories from the distant past.
senses.exampleCN: 那些是很久以前的故事。
senses.why: Memory thins the years the way fog thins a hill.
senses.whyCN: 记忆把年月磨淡，就像雾把山磨淡。

senses.title: Cool and not quite present
senses.definition: not friendly, or not paying attention to what is here
senses.definitionCN: 不亲近，或没有把心思放在眼前
senses.example: She gave a distant nod and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡地点了下头就走了。
senses.why: A mind can move far away while the body stays in the chair.
senses.whyCN: 人还坐在椅子上，心思却能走得很远。

intro.en: Distant is the Latin present participle distans, from distare, to stand apart, built on dis- and stare.
intro.cn: distant 是拉丁语现在分词 distans，来自 distare（相隔而立），由 dis- 与 stare 组成。

items.en: Stare meant to stand and keep a place.
items.cn: stare 指站着并守住一个位置。

items.en: Dis- marked the space between the two places.
items.cn: dis- 标出两处之间的间隔。

items.en: Distans described things that stood far from each other.
items.cn: distans 描述彼此站得很远的东西。

items.en: English used it first for places on a map.
items.cn: 英语先用它说地图上的地点。

items.en: It spread to years, relatives and cool manners.
items.cn: 后来扩展到年月、亲戚与冷淡的举止。

items.en: A distant look now means a mind somewhere else.
items.cn: 今天 a distant look 指心思飘在别处。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the same standing stem, while the meaning group gathers words for far and unfriendly.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」这段词干，近义组则是几个表示远与冷淡的词。

entries.definition: the space between two points
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间

entries.definition: in a far or cool manner
entries.definitionCN: 遥远或冷淡地

entries.definition: equally far from two points
entries.definitionCN: 与两点距离相等

entries.definition: a long way away
entries.definitionCN: 很远

entries.definition: far from towns and hard to reach
entries.definitionCN: 偏远而难到达

entries.definition: friendly in no obvious way
entries.definitionCN: 不亲近的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a small point on the horizon and end with a mind that has left the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地平线上的一个小点开始，落到一颗已经离屋的心思。

normal.en: Dis- plus stant: the two standing points are far apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stant，两个站立的点隔得很开。

normal.en: A distant light on the coast means the harbour is still far.
normal.cn: 海岸上远远一盏灯，说明港口还远。

normal.en: Letters from a distant cousin arrived once a year.
normal.cn: 远房表亲的信一年来一封。

normal.en: His voice went distant when the subject came up.
normal.cn: 话题一提起，他的声音就远了。

normal.en: She seemed distant, as if listening to another room.
normal.cn: 她显得心不在焉，像在听另一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a tower shrinking to a dot in fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔在雾里缩成一个小点。

abstract.en: Picture an old photograph with faces too small to name.
abstract.cn: 想象一张老照片，脸小得认不出。

abstract.en: Picture a person answering a question a second late.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人回答问题时慢了一拍。

examples.en: The distant mountains were lost in cloud.
examples.cn: 远处的山隐进云里。

examples.en: A distant train sounded across the valley.
examples.cn: 一列火车的声音从山谷那头传来。

examples.en: He was polite but distant with strangers.
examples.cn: 他对陌生人客气而疏远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distant 记成「站得远」：dis 表示分开，stant 与 stand 同源表示站着，站得开，就是远的，也可以指心思离得远。

root: 源自拉丁语 distare（相隔而立），由 dis-（分开）与 stare（站立）构成，现在分词为 distans。本义是位置离得远，后来用于时间上的久远，再引申为人情上的冷淡与心思上的不专注。

sensesIntro.en: From a hill far beyond the river to a face that answers you from a great distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从河那边很远的山，到一张仿佛从很远处回答你的脸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower on a hill shrinking into a dot in the fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：山上的塔在雾里缩成一个小点。

branches.en: The first sense is simple physical separation.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是单纯的空间相隔。

branches.en: The second sense measures separation in years.
branches.cn: 第二个义项用年月来量这段相隔。

branches.en: The third sense measures it in warmth between people.
branches.cn: 第三个义项用人与人之间的温度来量。

branches.en: Both senses keep one thing out of easy reach.
branches.cn: 两个义项都让某样东西不容易够到。

branches.en: Both senses grow stronger the longer nothing is said.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是越久不开口，就越显得明显。

intro.en: Distant gathers the stance family, where Latin stare, to stand, holds the stem steady.
intro.cn: distant 聚起 stance 一族，中心是拉丁语 stare（站立），把词干稳稳撑住。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, to stand, gives stance and distant; dis- turns standing together into standing apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stare（站立）给出 stance 与 distant，前缀 dis- 把站在一起变成站得很开。

items.meaning: in a far or cool way

items.example: The town is equidistant from both ports.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇到两个港口等距。
她把所有对手都甩开了。

items.meaning: the conditions standing around an event

definition_zh: 资格；资历；证书；限定条件；保留意见；（语法）修饰；（体育）预选赛
definition_en: a skill, certificate or condition that makes someone suitable, or a limitation added to a statement
core_image: 在一张表上逐格打钩，够格的人才被放进候选名单
scene: 这份工作要求有教师资格，还要至少两年的课堂教学经验。 The job requires a teaching qualification and at least two years of classroom experience.
sceneCN: 这里 qualification 是「资格证书」（第 2 个义项：证明具备任教资历的正式凭证）；句意：这份工作要求具备教师资格证书，以及至少两年的课堂经验。图中可辨识物件：盖章的证书、勾选过的条件清单；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Being fit for a role
senses.definition: the skills, knowledge or experience that make a person suitable for a job or role
senses.definitionCN: 使人适合某项工作或角色的技能、知识或经验
senses.example: Her qualifications for the post include six years of field research.
senses.exampleCN: 她胜任这一职位的资历包括六年实地研究经验。
senses.why: Qualis asked 'of what kind' and facere meant 'make'. To qualify is to make someone of the right kind for a role, and the noun names that fitness.
senses.whyCN: qualis 问“何种”，facere 意为“使”。qualify 就是使人变成适合某角色的那种类型，名词命名的正是这种适合。

senses.title: A certificate that proves it
senses.definition: an official certificate, degree or licence showing that a person has met a standard
senses.definitionCN: 证明某人达到某项标准的正式证书、学位或执照
senses.example: The clinic hires only nurses with a recognised qualification.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所只聘用持有认可资格证书的护士。
senses.why: The abstract fitness became a paper object: the certificate stands in for the training so an employer can check it quickly.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的适合变成一张纸：证书代替培训过程，让雇主能快速核查。

senses.title: A limit on a claim
senses.definition: a condition or limitation attached to a statement, making it narrower or less absolute
senses.definitionCN: 附加在陈述上的条件或限制，使其范围更窄或不再绝对
senses.example: He accepted the plan with one qualification: the budget must not exceed ten million.
senses.exampleCN: 他接受这项计划，但有一个限定条件：预算不得超过一千万。
senses.why: Qualis asks 'of what kind'. Here the kind is narrowed: the acceptance is not absolute but of one specific, limited kind, and the clause states the limit.
senses.whyCN: qualis 问“何种”。这里种类被收窄：接受不是绝对的，而是某个特定、有限的种类，而那个从句说明了限度。

senses.title: The act of becoming fit
senses.definition: the process of training or being certified as suitable for a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为胜任某一职业而接受培训或被认证的过程
senses.example: Qualification as a midwife takes three years in that country.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个国家，取得助产士资格需要三年。
senses.why: The noun also names the journey rather than the endpoint: the training, examinations and supervised practice that produce a qualified person.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也命名过程而非终点：产生合格者的培训、考试与督导实习。

senses.title: Grammar: narrowing a noun
senses.definition: the act of a word or phrase limiting or describing another word
senses.definitionCN: 词或短语限制、描述另一词的作用
senses.example: In 'the red door', 'red' performs a qualification of 'door'.
senses.exampleCN: 在“那扇红门”中，“红”对“门”起限定修饰作用。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the limiting sense: the modifier says what kind of door is meant, cutting the noun down from all doors to one described kind.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了限制义：修饰语说明指的是哪一种门，把名词从所有门收窄到被描述的那一种。

senses.title: A round before the main event
senses.definition: a preliminary stage in which competitors earn the right to enter the main competition
senses.definitionCN: 参赛者争取进入正赛资格的预赛阶段
senses.example: She finished second in the qualification and reached the final.
senses.exampleCN: 她在预选赛中名列第二，进入了决赛。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the fitness idea: a qualification round decides who is fit to enter the main draw.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了“适合”的观念：预选赛决定谁有资格进入正赛。

senses.title: Agreement with reservations
senses.definition: approval given with stated doubts or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在说明疑虑或条件的前提下给予赞同
senses.example: The committee gave its qualification rather than outright support.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会给出的是有保留的认可，而非无条件支持。
senses.why: Approval is granted, but as a qualified kind: the doubts are stated at the same time, so the support is real yet bounded.
senses.whyCN: 认可被给予了，但属于带限定的一类：疑虑同时被说明，因此支持是真的，却有边界。

senses.title: A restricting clause in law
senses.definition: a clause that limits the scope of a right, rule or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 限制某项权利、规则或协议范围的条款
senses.example: The lease contains a qualification on subletting the premises.
senses.exampleCN: 租约中有一条关于转租房屋的限制条款。
senses.why: Law states the limits explicitly: the clause makes the tenant's right a particular, restricted kind rather than an unrestricted one.
senses.whyCN: 法律把限度明说出来：这条使租客的权利成为某种特定、受限的类型，而非不受限制的类型。

intro.en: Qualification comes from Medieval Latin qualificatio, built on qualificare, 'to make of a certain kind'. Qualis meant 'of what kind' and facere meant 'to make'. The word began in scholastic philosophy as the assigning of a quality and later became the everyday word for fitness, certificates and reservations.
intro.cn: qualification 来自中古拉丁 qualificatio，建于 qualificare“使成为某种”之上。qualis 意为“何种”，facere 意为“使”。这个词始于经院哲学中“赋予性质”的用法，后来成为表示适合、证书与保留意见的日常词。

items.en: Qualis was the interrogative and relative word for 'of what kind'. It is the partner of quantus 'how much', and the pair still organizes scientific vocabulary.
items.cn: qualis 是表示“何种”的疑问与关系词，与 quantus“多少”配对，这对搭配至今组织着科学词汇。

items.en: Facere meant 'to make, to do'. Added to a stem, -ficare built verbs of making, as in aedificare and modificare.
items.cn: facere 意为“做、造”。加在词干后，-ficare 构成表示“使……”的动词，如 aedificare、modificare。

items.en: Scholastic Latin formed qualificare, 'to make of a certain quality or kind'. It was used for describing and for assigning properties.
items.cn: 经院拉丁语造出 qualificare“使具有某种性质或种类”，用于描述与赋予属性。

items.en: The noun qualificatio named the act of assigning a quality, and English took it up in the 15th century.
items.cn: 名词 qualificatio 命名赋予性质的行为，英语在 15 世纪吸收了它。

items.en: Legal and professional usage gave the word its two modern poles: being fit for an office, and adding a limiting condition to a claim.
items.cn: 法律与职业用法赋予这个词两个现代极点：适合某一职位，以及给陈述加上限制条件。

items.en: Public examinations made the certificate sense dominant, and sport adopted qualification for the preliminary round.
items.cn: 公共考试使证书义成为主流，体育则用 qualification 指预赛轮。

note.en: The look-alike group separates qualification from qualify, qualified and the quantity word quantification, which has a different root. The meaning group compares credentials, conditions and restrictions.
note.cn: 形近组区分 qualification 与 qualify、qualified，以及词根不同的 quantification；词义组比较资历凭证、条件与限制。

entries.definition: to become fit, to make someone fit, or to limit a statement. It is the action behind every sense of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 取得资格、使合格，或限定陈述。它是名词各义项背后的动作。

entries.definition: having the needed training, or stated with reservations. It describes the person or the approval.
entries.definitionCN: 具备所需训练，或有保留地表述的。它描述人或认可。

entries.definition: a word that limits another word, or a preliminary match. It names the limiter or the round, not the whole status.
entries.definitionCN: 限定另一词的词，或预赛。它命名限定成分或轮次，而非整体资格。

entries.definition: the act of measuring as a quantity. It looks similar but uses quantus 'how much', not qualis 'of what kind'.
entries.definitionCN: 按数量测量的行为。它看起来相似，却用 quantus“多少”，而非 qualis“何种”。

entries.definition: a qualification or document that proves trustworthiness. It is close to sense 02 but often implies proof of standing.
entries.definitionCN: 证明可信度的资格或文件。它接近第 2 义项，但常暗含地位证明。

entries.definition: the process or document of official certification. It stresses the authority that grants it.
entries.definitionCN: 官方认证的过程或文件。它强调授予认证的权威。

entries.definition: a warning or condition attached to a statement. It is the sharp word for sense 03.
entries.definitionCN: 附在陈述上的警告或条件。它是第 3 义项的锐利说法。

entries.definition: a rule that limits what may be done. It is the strongest word for sense 08.
entries.definitionCN: 限制可做之事的规则。它是第 8 义项最强的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the checklist image, then let the same word cover a certificate, a doubt, a training path, a modifier, a prelim, a reservation and a clause.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从勾选清单的画面出发，再让同一个词覆盖证书、疑虑、培训路径、修饰语、预赛、保留意见与条款。

normal.en: Split it as qual + i + fic + ation: what kind + make + noun. It names the making of a right kind of person.
normal.cn: 拆成 qual + i + fic + ation：何种、使、名词。它命名把人变成合适类型的过程。

normal.en: Picture a form with boxes to tick: only the person who fills every box enters the shortlist.
normal.cn: 想象一张打钩的表：填满每一格的人才进候选名单。

normal.en: The ticked form then becomes a certificate on the wall.
normal.cn: 这张勾好的表后来变成挂在墙上的证书。

normal.en: A qualification on a promise is a small box left unticked: agreement with one exception.
normal.cn: 承诺上的限定就是留空的一小格：同意，但有一个例外。

normal.en: A qualification round is the same shortlist, moved to a sports field.
normal.cn: 预选赛就是同一份候选名单，被搬到了运动场。

abstract.en: Hear the -fic- inside: the word is always about making someone or something fit a kind.
abstract.cn: 听见词里的 -fic-：这个词总是在讲使人或物适合某一类型。

abstract.en: Notice the two directions: outward proof (certificate) and inward limit (reservation).
abstract.cn: 注意两个方向：向外的证明（证书）与向内的限制（保留）。

abstract.en: Keep it away from quantification: one asks 'what kind', the other 'how much'.
abstract.cn: 把它与 quantification 分开：一个问“何种”，一个问“多少”。

examples.en: The fellowship lists a doctorate as a minimum qualification.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金把博士学位列为最低资格。

examples.en: She agreed to chair the panel, with the qualification that she could leave early.
examples.cn: 她同意主持专家组，但附带一个条件：她可以提前离场。

examples.en: Our team was eliminated in the qualification for the regional cup.
examples.cn: 我们队在地区杯的预选赛中被淘汰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“夸利非凯神”：夸你条件好、学历够，一张证书就神气起来。

root: 中古拉丁 qualificare“使成为某种”（qualis 何种 + facere 使）的名词 qualificatio；核心是“把人或物变成合适的类型”。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all concern fitness: the skills that fit a role, the paper that proves it, the training that produces it, the doubt that limits an agreement, the modifier that narrows a noun, the round that decides who may compete, the reservation on approval, and the clause that limits a right.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都关乎“适合”：适合某一角色的技能、证明它的纸、产生它的训练、限制协议的疑虑、收窄名词的修饰语、决定谁可参赛的轮次、认可上的保留，以及限制权利的条款。

core.en: A person or statement is narrowed to fit a standard, and the fit is then certified or limited.
core.cn: 人或陈述被收窄到符合某一标准，随后这种符合被认证或被限制。

branches.en: FITNESS: skills and a certificate show that a person suits a role.
branches.cn: 适合：技能与证书表明一个人适合某角色。

branches.en: LIMIT: agreement is narrowed by a stated condition.
branches.cn: 限制：同意被明说的条件收窄。

branches.en: PROCESS: training and examination produce the fit kind of person.
branches.cn: 过程：培训与考试产生合适类型的人。

branches.en: SCOPE: a modifier or a legal clause cuts down what the words cover.
branches.cn: 范围：修饰语或法律条款削减文字覆盖的范围。

branches.en: COMPETITION: a preliminary round decides who is fit to enter.
branches.cn: 竞争：预赛决定谁有资格进入。

intro.en: Qualification is qualis plus facere plus the noun suffix -atio. The items below follow the same making verb through verb, adjective, agent and the parallel quantity family.
intro.cn: qualification 由 qualis、facere 与名词后缀 -atio 构成。下列条目沿着同一个“使”动词，走过动词、形容词、施动者，以及平行的数量词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the kind word and the making verb. They explain why qualification, quality and qualify all turn on 'what kind'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“何种”与“使”两个词，解释为什么 qualification、quality 与 qualify 都围绕“何种”。

items.example: The certificate is a formal qualification.
items.exampleCN: 这张证书是正式资格证明。

items.meaning: to make or become fit; to limit
items.example: Two years of practice qualify her for the licence.
items.exampleCN: 两年实践使她符合执照要求。
专家组给予了有保留的支持。

items.meaning: a limiting word; a preliminary round
items.example: In the phrase, the adjective is a qualifier.
items.exampleCN: 在该短语中，形容词是限定成分。

items.meaning: the kind or character of something
items.example: The quality of the soil improved.
The study relied on qualitative evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究依靠定性证据。

items.meaning: the loss of fitness or the act of removing it
items.exampleCN: 这次犯规导致取消资格。

items.example: Nurses complete requalification every three years.
items.exampleCN: 护士每三年完成一次资格复审。

latinEntries.meaning: a making of a certain kind

definition_zh: 离开；出发；背离
definition_en: the act of leaving a place, or a change away from what is usual
core_image: 机场大屏上一行行航班变成灰色，登机口空了下来
scene: 广播念出航班号，候机的人陆续站起来，椅子一排排空下去。 Her departure left the office very quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 departure 指「离开」（第 1 个义项：离开某地的行为）；句意是她的离开让办公室安静下来。

derivatives.zh: 离开；出发
已故的

senses.title: The act of leaving
senses.definition: the act of going away from a place
senses.definitionCN: 从某地走开的行为
senses.example: Her departure left the office very quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 她的离开让办公室安静下来。
senses.why: A leaving is felt most by the people who stay.
senses.whyCN: 离开这件事，留在原地的人感受最深。

senses.title: The start of a journey
senses.definition: the moment when a journey or flight begins
senses.definitionCN: 旅程或航班开始的时刻
senses.example: The departure time is printed on the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 票上印着出发时间。
senses.why: A journey has to be dated from somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 旅程总得从一个时刻算起。

senses.title: A turn away from the old
senses.definition: a change that leaves the usual way behind
senses.definitionCN: 离开通常做法的改变
senses.example: The new design is a departure from tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 新设计是对传统的一次背离。
senses.why: Not every departure needs a station; an idea can leave too.
senses.whyCN: 不是每次离开都需要车站，想法也会出走。

intro.en: Departure grew from French départir, to divide or leave, and added the noun ending -ure.
intro.cn: departure 从法语 départir（划分、离开）长出来，后面加了名词词尾 -ure。

items.en: Departir meant to divide, to separate or to leave.
items.cn: departir 表示划分、分开或离开。

items.en: Departure named a separation or a going away.
items.cn: departure 指一次分离或一次走开。

items.en: English used departure for the act of leaving.
items.cn: 英语用 departure 表示离开这一行为。

items.en: Travel gave it a fixed place beside arrival.
items.cn: 旅行让它与到达并列，各占一头。

items.en: Now it also covers leaving a job or an old method.
items.cn: 如今它也指离开一份工作或一种旧方法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the depart stem, and the meaning group names leaving from several angles.
note.cn: 形近组共用 depart 词干，近义组则从几个角度说离开。

entries.definition: to leave a place
entries.definitionCN: 离开某地

entries.definition: one part of a large organization
entries.definitionCN: 大机构划分出的一个部分

entries.definition: about to leave
entries.definitionCN: 即将离开的

entries.definition: the act of going out
entries.definitionCN: 走出去的行为

entries.definition: the act of saying goodbye and going
entries.definitionCN: 道别并离开的行为

entries.definition: the act of moving back or out
entries.definitionCN: 退回或退出的行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a board of greyed-out flights and end with an idea walking away from an old rule.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一块变灰的航班牌开始，落到一个离开旧规则的想法。

normal.en: An empty gate is a departure you can see.
normal.cn: 空着的登机口，是一场看得见的离开。

normal.en: A ticket has two times: one for leaving, one for arriving.
normal.cn: 一张票有两个时间：一个离开，一个到达。

normal.en: The people who stay hear the door close longest.
normal.cn: 留在原地的人，听关门声听得最久。

normal.en: A departure from tradition needs no suitcase.
normal.cn: 背离传统，不需要行李箱。

normal.en: Departure is the noun that turns departing into a thing.
normal.cn: departure 就是把离开变成一件事的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a row of chairs with coats lifted off them.
abstract.cn: 想象一排椅子，上面的外套被一件件拿走。

abstract.en: Picture a gate number still glowing after the flight has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象航班走了，登机口号码还亮着。

abstract.en: Picture a road forking away from a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路从直线上岔开。

examples.en: Her departure left the office very quiet.
examples.cn: 她的离开让办公室安静下来。

examples.en: The departure time is printed on the ticket.
examples.cn: 票上印着出发时间。

examples.en: The new design is a departure from tradition.
examples.cn: 新设计是对传统的一次背离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 departure 记成「分开的车」：depart 是离开，ure 是名词尾，车一开走，就是一场离开。

root: 来自法语 départir（划分、离开）加名词词尾 -ure。它先指一次分离或走开，十五世纪进入英语，十七世纪随着旅行文学与到达并列，现代又引申为离开职位与背离旧法。

sensesIntro.en: From a gate that empties, to a time printed on a ticket, to a design that leaves the old path.
sensesIntro.cn: 从空下来的登机口，到票上印着的时间，再到离开旧路的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate number glows above a row of empty chairs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排空椅子上方，登机口号码还亮着。

branches.en: The first sense is the plain fact of someone going.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是有人走了这个朴素事实。

branches.en: The second sense is the clock time when a journey starts.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是旅程开始的钟点。

branches.en: The third sense is a method or habit left behind.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被留在身后的方法或习惯。

branches.en: Every journey begins as a leaving, with a time attached.
branches.cn: 每段旅程都从一次离开开始，还带着一个时间。

branches.en: A person and a design can both depart from what was expected.
branches.cn: 人与设计，都可能从预期里走出去。

intro.en: Departure is the noun of leaving, standing beside depart and the whole parting family.
intro.cn: departure 是表示离开的名词，与 depart 以及整个「分开」家族站在一起。

latinIntro.en: The base is partire, to divide; -ure turns the act into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 partire（划分），-ure 把这个动作变成名词。

definition_zh: 敏感的；易受影响的；灵敏的；体贴的
definition_en: quick to feel, notice, or be affected by something
core_image: 含羞草的叶子，指尖一碰就轻轻合拢
scene: 递问卷前，护士特意放轻了语气。 The nurse asked the sensitive question in a very quiet voice.
sceneCN: 这里 sensitive 是「敏感的；需谨慎处理的」（第 4 个义项：易触痛、须小心）；句意是护士用极轻的语气提出那个敏感问题。

derivatives.zh: sensitive 加 -ity 名词后缀，义为「敏感性；灵敏度」
sensitive 动词化，义为「使敏感」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「不敏感的；麻木的」

senses.title: Quick to react to physical things
senses.definition: reacting strongly to touch, light, cold, or substances
senses.definitionCN: 对触碰、光线、寒冷或物质反应强烈
senses.example: Her sensitive skin reddens in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 她的敏感肌肤在阳光下会发红。
senses.why: The mimosa leaf folds before the finger even lands.
senses.whyCN: 指尖未落，含羞草叶已合拢。

senses.title: Able to notice feelings
senses.titleCN: 善解人意的；情感敏锐的
senses.definition: good at understanding other people's emotions
senses.definitionCN: 善于察觉他人情绪
senses.example: A sensitive teacher notices the silent student.
senses.exampleCN: 敏锐的老师会注意到沉默的学生。
senses.why: The leaf also trembles when only the wind changes.
senses.whyCN: 风声刚变，叶已轻颤。

senses.title: Reacting strongly to art or ideas
senses.definition: appreciating art, beauty, or ideas deeply
senses.definitionCN: 深刻领会艺术、美或思想
senses.example: He gives a sensitive reading of the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这首诗的解读极具感受力。
senses.why: The leaf opens fully to the morning light
senses.whyCN: 叶面对晨光全然舒展。

senses.title: Easily harmed; needing careful handling
