senses.title: Advance someone in rank
senses.definition: to move a person to a higher position or rank
senses.definitionCN: 把某人移到更高的职位或等级
senses.example: She was promoted to department head.
senses.exampleCN: 她被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Latin promovere means 'move forward': pro- 'forward' plus movere 'to move'. A promotion moves a person up the institutional ladder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 promovere 意为“向前移动”：pro-“向前”加 movere“移动”。晋升就是把一个人沿机构的梯子往上移。

senses.title: Encourage growth or success
senses.definition: to help something grow, develop, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某事物成长、发展或成功
senses.example: The policy promotes small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策促进小企业。
senses.why: The object changes from a person to a process: what is promoted is made to move forward. The word becomes a general verb of support.
senses.whyCN: 对象从人变成过程：被 promote 的东西被推着向前。这个词变成泛用的支持动词。

senses.title: Advertise or publicize
senses.definition: to make a product, idea, or event known in order to sell or gain support
senses.definitionCN: 使产品、理念或活动为人所知，以销售或争取支持
senses.example: The company promotes its new phone online.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在网上推销新手机。
senses.why: Commerce borrows the ladder image: a product is moved forward in the market, pushed toward buyers. Promotion becomes the noun of marketing.
senses.whyCN: 商业借来梯子意象：产品在市场中被向前推，推向买家。promotion 于是成了营销名词。

senses.title: Move a pupil to the next grade
senses.definition: to advance a student to the next class or level
senses.definitionCN: 把学生升到下一个班级或年级
senses.example: All students were promoted to the next grade.
senses.exampleCN: 所有学生都升到了下一个年级。
senses.why: Schools use the same upward motion: a pupil moves from one level to the next. The opposite, to hold back, keeps the spatial logic.
senses.whyCN: 学校用同一个向上运动：学生从一级移到下一级。反义词“留级”保留同样的空间逻辑。

senses.title: Cause an idea or cause to advance
senses.definition: to help a cause, idea, or value become stronger or more accepted
senses.definitionCN: 帮助事业、理念或价值变得更强、更被接受
senses.example: The campaign promotes healthy eating.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动推广健康饮食。
senses.why: Public language treats values as objects that can be pushed forward. To promote peace is to give it momentum in the world.
senses.whyCN: 公共语言把价值当作可被推向前方的物体。promote peace 就是让和平在世界上获得动量。

senses.title: Advance a pawn in chess
senses.definition: in chess, to move a pawn to the last rank and replace it with a stronger piece
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中，把兵走到对方底线并换成更强的子
senses.example: The pawn was promoted to a queen.
senses.exampleCN: 那个兵升变为后。
senses.why: Chess gives the ladder literal form: a lowly pawn reaches the far rank and becomes a queen. The metaphor of advancement becomes a rule of the game.
senses.whyCN: 国际象棋把梯子变成字面规则：卑微的兵走到远端，变成后。“晋升”隐喻成了游戏规则。

senses.title: Move a team to a higher league
senses.definition: in sport, to move a club or player to a higher division
senses.definitionCN: 体育中把俱乐部或选手升到更高级别
senses.example: The club was promoted to the first division.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部升入甲级。
senses.why: League tables rank teams by results. Promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror. The word makes sport a visible ladder.
senses.whyCN: 联赛积分榜按成绩给球队排序。升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。这个词让体育成了一条可见的梯子。

senses.title: Accelerate a chemical reaction
senses.definition: in chemistry, to increase the rate of a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 化学中加快反应速率
senses.example: The catalyst promotes the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂促进该反应。
senses.why: A catalyst moves a reaction forward without being consumed. Science uses promote for any agent that speeds a process, keeping the 'move forward' core.
senses.whyCN: 催化剂推动反应向前，自身不被消耗。科学用 promote 指任何加速过程的因素，保留“向前移动”核心。

senses.title: Push forward physically (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, to move something forward in space
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：把某物在空间中向前推
senses.example: The crowd promoted him toward the door.
senses.exampleCN: 人群把他推向门口。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin sense, now rare. Modern English keeps it mainly in the abstract ladder, but the physical push is still visible in the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁字面义，现已罕见。现代英语主要在抽象梯子中保留它，但物理的“推”仍能在隐喻中看见。

intro.en: Promote is a forward-motion word: Latin promovere joins pro- 'forward' to movere 'to move'. English borrowed it in the late 14c. and then applied the same push to careers, causes, products, and pawns.
intro.cn: promote 是一个向前运动的词：拉丁语 promovere 把 pro-“向前”与 movere“移动”结合。英语在 14 世纪末借入，随后把同一推动用到职业、事业、产品与棋子。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'advance, further, encourage'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“推进、促进、鼓励”。

items.en: From Latin promovere 'move forward, advance, bring forward' = pro- 'forward' + movere 'to move'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 promovere“向前移、推进、带上前”= pro-“向前”+ movere“移动”。

items.en: movere also gives move, remove, motive, emotion, and moment. The family is about motion, and pro- turns it into forward motion.
items.cn: movere 还生成 move、remove、motive、emotion、moment。这个词族关乎运动，pro- 把它变成向前运动。

items.en: The senses 'raise to a higher office' and 'help forward a cause' become established.
items.cn: “提升到更高职位”与“推动某项事业”的义项确立。

items.en: Commercial promotion appears: advertising pushes goods toward buyers.
items.cn: 商业推广义出现：广告把商品推向买家。

items.en: Modern English uses promote for careers, health, products, teams, and chemical reactions, always with the same forward push.
items.cn: 现代英语用 promote 指职业、健康、产品、球队与化学反应，始终是同一个向前推动。

note.en: The first group shares the movere root and the -mote shape; the second is about verbs that also mean raising or supporting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 movere 词根与 -mote 形态，第二组看同样表示“提升”或“支持”的动词。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin movere 'move', the pro- 'forward' prefix, the promotion/promoter pair, and the chess and league uses.

normal.cn: movere 意为“移动”，pro- 意为“向前”：promote 就是把某人或某物向前移。

normal.en: The same push serves a career, a cause, a product, and a pawn: all are moved up or forward.

normal.cn: remote 是 re- 加 movere，“被移开”；promote 是 pro- 加 movere，“被推向前”。一个前缀，两个方向。

normal.en: In sport, promotion is the reward for finishing high, and relegation is its mirror image.
normal.cn: 体育中，升级是名列前茅的奖赏，降级是它的镜像。

normal.en: A catalyst promotes a reaction without being consumed: it pushes the process forward and stays.

abstract.en: To promote an idea is to give it momentum in other minds, not merely to mention it.
abstract.cn: 推动一个理念，是给它在他者心智中的动量，而不只是提到它。

abstract.en: The chess pawn shows the metaphor literally: the lowest piece can become the highest by reaching the far rank.

normal.en: Con- is together and cept is to take, so a concept is what the mind takes in together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，cept 是拿取，concept 就是心智一起收进来的东西。

normal.en: A concept is a box in the mind that holds many examples.
normal.cn: 概念是脑中的一只盒子，装着许多例子。

normal.en: Concept is the thing; conception is the act of forming it.
normal.cn: concept 是那个东西，conception 是形成它的动作。

normal.en: A concept car is a car that lives in the mind before the road.
normal.cn: 概念车是先活在脑中、后上路的汽车。

normal.en: Abstract concepts have no shape, so we borrow pictures for them.
normal.cn: 抽象概念没有形状，所以我们借图画来表现它们。

abstract.en: Picture many scattered dots joined by one thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多散点被一条细线连起来。

abstract.en: Picture a light bulb above a sketched machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一台草图机器上方亮起一只灯泡。

abstract.en: Picture a label that fits a whole shelf of jars.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签适合整架罐子。

examples.en: Children learn the concept of number before they write figures.
examples.cn: 孩子在写数字之前先学会数的概念。

examples.en: The designer explained her concept for the new library.
examples.cn: 设计师讲解了她对新图书馆的构想。

examples.en: It is a simple concept but hard to apply.
examples.cn: 这是个简单的概念，却很难应用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 concept 记成 con（一起）加 cept（拿取）：把许多例子一起收进脑子，就成了一个概念。

root: 源自拉丁语 concipere（com 一起 + capere 拿取）的过去分词 conceptum，本义是收入心智之物，后指概念与构想。

sensesIntro.en: From a general idea that gathers examples, to a design that exists before the object.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把例子收拢起来的一般想法，到先于实物存在的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thin line tying many scattered examples into a single knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细线把许多散开的例子系成一个结。

branches.en: The general idea is the central and most common sense.
branches.cn: 一般想法是核心也最常见的义项。

branches.en: The design sense narrows the idea to a future product.
branches.cn: 设计义项把想法收窄到未来的产品。

branches.en: Philosophers study concepts as units of thought.
branches.cn: 哲学家把概念当作思维单位来研究。

branches.en: Companies show concept models before they sell anything.
branches.cn: 公司在销售之前先展示概念模型。

branches.en: Both senses are things held in the mind before they are things in the world.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是先存在于脑中、后存在于世上的东西。

intro.en: Concept is built on Latin com-, together, plus capere, to take, through the form conceptum.
intro.cn: concept 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 capere（拿取）构成，形式为 conceptum。

latinIntro.en: The Latin take base cap- also gives capture, accept and capacity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的拿取词基 cap- 还给出 capture、accept 与 capacity。

items.example: Her conception of duty is strict.
items.exampleCN: 她对责任的理解很严格。
这张图仍停留在概念阶段。

items.example: The two plans are conceptually similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个方案在概念上相似。

items.meaning: to form an idea of something
items.example: It is hard to conceptualize such a large number.
items.exampleCN: 很难构想这么大的数字。

items.example: The book offers a new conceptualization of space.
items.exampleCN: 这本书提供了对空间的新概念化。
他写过关于中世纪概念论的文章。

items.example: They misconceive the purpose of the rule.
items.exampleCN: 他们误解了这条规则的目的。

definition_zh: 管理；行政；政府；给药；施行
definition_en: the work of managing an organization or public affairs, the government of a country, or the act of giving a drug or putting a law into effect
core_image: 桌子后面的人把任务、文件和物资一一分派到各个岗位
scene: 夜班病房里，护士推着小车按医嘱逐床分发药片。 The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
sceneCN: 这里 administration 是「给药、用药」（第 4 个义项：把药物给予病人）；句意为护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。

pos.zh: 名词：管理、经营；行政；政府；给药；施行

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾而来，义为「管理；施行；给药」
由本词加形容词词尾 -ive 构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加动词词尾 -ate 构成，义为「管理；经营」

senses.title: The work of managing an organization
senses.definition: the activity of organizing and running an institution, company or project
senses.definitionCN: 组织和运营机构、公司或项目的活动
senses.example: She studied business administration at a college in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方一所学院学习工商管理。
senses.why: Latin administrare meant 'to serve, carry out', and running an institution is service done on its behalf rather than for oneself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 administrare 意为「服务、执行」：经营一个机构，就是替它做事、替它把事务办成，而不是替自己办事。

senses.title: Public administration; the work of government
senses.definition: the activity of managing public affairs and putting government policy into practice
senses.definitionCN: 管理公共事务、把政府政策付诸实施的活动
senses.example: Better public administration would shorten the queues at the office.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的公共行政能缩短办事窗口前的排队。
senses.why: Serving the state is the same service, only the master is now the public; administrare applied to the commonwealth becomes 'administration'.
senses.whyCN: 为国家做事还是同一件「服务」，只是主人换成了公众；administrare 一旦用到公共事务上，就成了「行政」。

senses.title: A government in office
senses.definition: the group of people who run a country at a particular time, especially in the United States
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期执掌国家的一批人，尤用于美国的说法
senses.example: The new administration promised to reform the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届政府承诺改革税制。
senses.why: The people who carry out the state's business are named after the activity itself, so the whole government takes the word for its work.
senses.whyCN: 负责替国家办事的那批人，直接用这项活动的名字来称呼；于是整个政府就用「工作」之名来指代。

senses.title: The giving of a drug
senses.definition: the act of giving a medicine or treatment to a patient, especially in a controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或治疗给予病人，尤指按规范进行
senses.example: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。
senses.why: To administer once meant 'to hand out, dispense'; giving a dose is that old sense of handing something over, surviving in medical usage.
senses.whyCN: administer 原本有「分发、施予」的意思；把一剂药发到病人手上，正是这个旧义在医学语境里的延续。

senses.title: The carrying out of a law, oath or rite
senses.titleCN: 施行；执行（法律、誓言、仪式）
senses.definition: the act of formally putting into effect something such as justice, an oath or a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式使司法、誓言或仪式等生效的行为
senses.example: The administration of justice requires courts that are free from pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 司法要求法院不受压力干扰。
senses.why: Service hardens into execution: the official is the one who carries a rule or a rite all the way through to its end.
senses.whyCN: 「服务」进一步硬化成「执行」：官员的职责就是把一条规则或一项仪式从头办到底。

intro.en: Administration is Latin ad- plus ministrare 'to serve', and the whole family keeps the image of service carried out for someone else.
intro.cn: administration 是拉丁语 ad- 加 ministrare「服务」构成的，整个词族都保留着「替别人把事办成」的画面。

items.en: Minister meant 'servant, attendant', and it is generally connected with minus 'less'.
items.cn: minister 意为「仆人、随从」，一般认为与 minus「较少」有关。

items.en: Ministrare meant 'to serve, attend to, manage', and was formed from minister.
items.cn: ministrare 意为「服务、照料、料理」，由 minister 构成。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus ministrare formed administrare, 'to serve, manage, carry out'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: The noun administratio meant 'management, service, execution', and English took it through Old French.
items.cn: 名词 administratio 意为「管理、服务、执行」，英语经古法语把它借入。

items.en: Recorded in English in the fourteenth century for the managing of affairs; the medical and governmental senses developed later, and the exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪用它表示事务管理；医学义与政府义后来才发展出来，确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word family built on the same serving root; the near-meaning group holds words for running affairs, for government, and for a measured amount of medicine.
note.cn: 形近组是建立在同一「服务」词根上的词族；近义组收表示管理事务、治理国家与药物用量的词。

entries.definition: To manage affairs, to put a law into effect, or to give a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、施行、给药」，与本词同出拉丁语 administrare。

entries.definition: Relating to the managing of an organization or to routine office work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、事务性的」，由本词加形容词词尾构成。

entries.definition: A person who manages the day-to-day running of an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」，由本词加表示人的后缀构成。

entries.definition: A senior government official or a clergy member; literally a servant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部长、牧师」，字面意思是「仆人」，与本词共享同一个词根。

entries.definition: The process of running a business or team; closer to the everyday work than to public affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、经营」，偏指企业与团队的日常运作，不含政府义。

entries.definition: The group of people who govern a country, or the system by which it is governed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「政府、政体」，是比 administration 更中性的通用说法。

entries.definition: The way in which an organization or country is controlled and directed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「治理、治理方式」，强调运作机制本身，而不是执行事务的机构。

entries.definition: A measured quantity of a medicine taken at one time; the amount, not the act of giving it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一剂、剂量」，指一次服用的药量，而 administration 指给药这个动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root minister 'servant' and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 minister「仆人」，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Minister is a servant: administration is service carried out on behalf of an institution.
normal.cn: minister 是「仆人」：administration 就是替一个机构办事的服务。

normal.en: The same root gives minister, ministry, administer and administrator.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 minister、ministry、administer 与 administrator。

normal.en: Public administration is service to the public, not private business.
normal.cn: public administration 是对公众的服务，而不是私人生意。

normal.en: In medicine, administration names the giving of the dose, not the dose itself.
normal.cn: 在医学里，administration 指把药给出去这个动作，而不是那一剂药本身。

normal.en: The administration of justice means carrying the law through, not writing it.
normal.cn: the administration of justice 指把法律执行到底，而不是制定法律。

abstract.en: Picture a servant walking a tray of papers down a corridor, handing each sheet to the right desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一个仆人端着一盘文件走过走廊，把每张纸递到该去的桌子。

abstract.en: The tray can hold tasks, money, laws or medicine: the word stays the same because the gesture is the same.
abstract.cn: 那只托盘里可以装任务、钱、法律或药：动作没变，词也就不变。

abstract.en: From behind the desk, the servant slowly becomes the one who decides, which is how the word also comes to mean a government.
abstract.cn: 从桌子后面开始，仆人慢慢变成拍板的人，这个词因此也能指一届政府。

examples.en: She studied business administration at a college in the north.
examples.cn: 她在北方一所学院学习工商管理。

examples.en: The new administration promised to reform the tax system.
examples.cn: 新一届政府承诺改革税制。

examples.en: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug in the ward log.
examples.cn: 护士把给药情况记进了病房记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼」——阿德把米一份份分给众人：管理、行政，也指给药。

root: 拉丁语 administratio，由 ad-「朝向」+ ministrare「服务」构成，ministrare 又出自 minister「仆人、随从」；核心意思是替他人把事务办成。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of administration come from serving: serving an institution, serving the public, the people who serve as a government, and the handing over of a drug or a legal act.
sensesIntro.cn: administration 的五个义项都从「服务」长出来：替机构办事、替公众办事、替公众办事的那批人，以及把药物或法律行为交出去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person behind a table handing out tasks, papers and supplies to each post.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子后面的人把任务、文件和物资一一分派到各个岗位。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: serving an organization gradually turns into running it.
branches.cn: 机构线：替一个机构办事，渐渐就变成经营它。

branches.en: PUBLIC AFFAIRS: the same service aimed at the state becomes administration.
branches.cn: 公共线：同样的服务对准国家，就成了行政。

branches.en: GOVERNMENT: the people who carry out public business are named after the work itself.
branches.cn: 政府线：替公众办事的那批人，直接用这件工作的名字来称呼。

branches.en: MEDICINE: handing out a dose is the oldest dispensing strand of the word.
branches.cn: 医学线：把一剂药发出去，是这个词最古老的「分发」支脉。

branches.en: LAW AND RITE: carrying a rule or a ceremony through to the end.
branches.cn: 法律与仪式线：把一条规则或一项仪式从头办到底。

intro.en: Administration is a Latin verb plus a noun ending, carried into English through Old French; its parts still build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: administration 是拉丁语动词加名词词尾，经古法语进入英语；这些组成部分至今仍在构成同族的其他词。

latinIntro.en: Minister, ministrare, administrare and administratio are all recorded in Latin, so only the still older Indo-European layer would be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: minister、ministrare、administrare 与 administratio 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有更早的印欧层才属于重构。

items.example: It turns serving into serving towards someone.
items.exampleCN: 它把「服务」变成「朝着某人去服务」。

items.example: It is the human centre of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族里指人的核心。

items.example: It supplies the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: It adds the prefix to the verb of serving.
items.exampleCN: 它把前缀加到表示「服务」的动词上。

items.example: English took this noun through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 英语经古法语借入了这个名词。

items.example: It makes a noun of the act of managing.
items.exampleCN: 它把「管理」这一动作变成名词。

derivatives.zh: 由本词的拉丁动词形式而来，义为「管理；施行；给药」
由本词加后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加后缀 -ive 构成，义为「行政的；事务性的」

definition_zh: 不公平的；不公正的；偏袒的；违反规则的
definition_en: not fair, not based on equal treatment or on what is right or just
core_image: 一架秤，一边被悄悄压上了看不见的砝码
scene: 两条跑道一湿一干，起跑线前孩子们皱起了眉头。 It seemed unfair that one lane was dry and the other was soaked.
sceneCN: 这里 unfair 是形容词「不公平的」（第 1 个义项：待遇不平等）；句意为一条跑道干一条湿，这看起来不公平。

pos.zh: 不公平的；不公正的；偏袒的
违反规则或道德的；不正当的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「不公平地；不公正地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「不公平；不公正」
去掉否定前缀后的词基，义为「公平的；公正的」

senses.title: Not equal in treatment
senses.definition: treating people unequally when they should be treated the same
senses.definitionCN: 本应一视同仁时却区别对待
senses.example: It is unfair to judge two applicants by different standards.
senses.exampleCN: 用不同标准评判两位申请者是不公平的。
senses.why: Fair once meant beautiful and then levelled into even-handed; un- simply lifts the level out from under the scale.
senses.whyCN: fair 由「美丽」演化为「持平均匀」；un- 只是把秤下的水平面抽走。

senses.title: Not just or right
senses.definition: contrary to justice or to what is morally right
senses.definitionCN: 与正义或道德上正当之事相悖
senses.example: Punishing the whole class for one pupil's mistake was unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 因一名学生的过错惩罚全班是不公正的。
senses.why: A fair judgement weighs blame against deed; when the weights are wrong, the sentence itself tilts.
senses.whyCN: 公正的判决让过错与惩罚相称；砝码一旦放错，判决本身便倾斜了。

senses.title: Showing favouritism
senses.definition: favouring one side or person without good reason
senses.definitionCN: 没有正当理由地偏袒一方或某人
senses.example: The referee's unfair favouritism spoiled the whole match.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判不公的偏袒毁了整场比赛。
senses.why: A level field lets skill decide; favouritism is a hidden thumb on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 平整的场地让技艺决定胜负；偏袒是压在秤上的隐形拇指。

senses.title: Breaking the rules of a game
senses.definition: not allowed by the rules of a game or contest
senses.definitionCN: 为比赛或竞赛规则所不允许的
senses.example: It is unfair to start before the whistle blows.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声未响就抢先起跑是不合规则的。
senses.why: Games are fairness made visible: the rules are the level ground, and unfair play digs a hole in it.
senses.whyCN: 游戏是把公平变得可见的形式：规则就是平地，违规行为就是在平地上挖坑。

senses.title: Taking undue advantage
senses.definition: gaining an advantage by methods that equal rivals do not have
senses.definitionCN: 用对手无法享有的手段获取优势
senses.example: Using the leaked answers gave the team an unfair advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 使用泄露的答案让该队占了不公平的便宜。
senses.why: Advantage is fair when every runner starts at the same line; a head start no one else has is unfairness in inches.
senses.whyCN: 当每位跑者都站在同一条起跑线上时优势才是公平的；他人没有的先手就是以寸计的不公。

senses.title: Commercially improper
senses.definition: breaching accepted standards of business conduct, as in unfair competition
senses.definitionCN: 违背公认商业行为准则，如不正当竞争
senses.example: The court found the firm guilty of unfair competition.
senses.exampleCN: 法院判定该公司存在不正当竞争行为。
senses.why: Markets promise a fair ring: no tricks, no rigged weights; unfair practice is a weight palmed in the open square.
senses.whyCN: 市场承诺公平的交易：不耍花招、不压秤；不正当行为就是众目睽睽之下掌心藏着的砝码。

senses.title: Unjust criticism or blame
senses.definition: criticism or blame that does not match what was actually done
senses.definitionCN: 与实际所为不相称的批评或指责
senses.example: The paper later admitted its unfair attack on the young author.
senses.exampleCN: 该报后来承认对那位年轻作者的攻击有失公允。
senses.why: Blame should weigh the deed, not the mood; an unfair accusation loads the scale with what never happened.
senses.whyCN: 指责应当衡量行为而非情绪；不公正的指控是往秤上放从未发生之事的砝码。

senses.title: In law: procedurally wrong
senses.definition: failing the required standards of a legal process, as in unfair dismissal or unfair trial
senses.definitionCN: 未达到法律程序要求的正当标准，如不公平解雇、审判不公
senses.example: The tribunal ruled the dismissal unfair and ordered compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 裁定机构认定解雇不公，判令给予补偿。
senses.why: Law formalises the scale: procedures are the pivot, and unfair procedure moves the pivot itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律把秤制度化：程序是支点，程序不公移动的正是支点本身。

intro.en: Unfair is the Old English pair fair plus un-, both layers native to English.
intro.cn: unfair 由 fair 加古英语前缀 un- 构成，两个层次都是英语本族成分。

items.en: *peh₂- is generally reconstructed as a root meaning the same in Old English and Old Saxon; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语重构词根 *peh₂- 在古英语与古撒克逊语中同义；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English fæge meant beautiful, pleasant, or fated to die; the modern senses of beautiful and fair-haired descend from it.
items.cn: 古英语 fæge 意为「美丽的；宜人的；注定一死的」，现代「美丽」「金发白皙」诸义皆源于此。

items.en: By the thirteenth century fair had widened to clean, unblemished, lawful, and then even-handed in judgement.
items.cn: 十三世纪时 fair 已扩展为「洁净的；无瑕的；合法的」，进而表示「评判持中的」。

items.en: The prefix un- is native Old English, cognate with Latin in- and Greek a(n)-, and attaches freely to adjectives.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 是古英语本族成分，与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源，可自由加于形容词前。

items.en: Unfair is recorded from Old English times in the sense not beautiful, and from Middle English in the modern sense not just.
items.cn: unfair 早在古英语时期已有记录，义为「不美的」；现代「不公」义自中古英语时期确立。

items.en: The word now anchors the vocabulary of justice: unfair treatment, unfair dismissal, unfair competition.
items.cn: 如今该词是正义词汇的基石：不公平对待、不公平解雇、不正当竞争。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fair family and un- counterparts; the near-meaning group gathers words for injustice and bias.
note.cn: 形近组收 fair 词族与 un- 对应词；近义组收不义与偏颇类词。

entries.definition: The positive base: just, even-handed, or blonde.
entries.definitionCN: 正面词基，义为「公平的；公正的；（发色）浅淡的」。

entries.definition: The adverb: justly, or simply quite.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「公正地」，也可弱化为「相当」。

entries.definition: The adverb of this entry: in an unjust way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不公平地」。

entries.definition: To get on, or a transport charge; same sound but a different word and origin, only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「进展；车费」，与 fair 同音但来源不同，只是音同形近。

entries.definition: Not suitable; built with the same un- prefix on a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合适的」，用同一 un- 前缀加于另一词根。

entries.definition: Contrary to justice; more formal and legal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不公正的」，语气更正式、更书面。

entries.definition: Leaning to one side in judgement; stresses the tilt itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有偏见的」，强调倾斜本身。

entries.definition: Favouring one side; the opposite of impartial.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偏袒的」，与 impartial 相对。

entries.definition: Not equitable; formal, used of distributions and arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不公平的」，正式用语，多指分配与安排。

entries.definition: Favouring only one view or party; everyday and vivid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「片面的；一边倒的」，日常且形象。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the prefix, the base, and the sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自前缀、词基与同音词的记忆锚点。

normal.en: Un- + fair: fair is the level scale, unfair is the loaded one.
normal.cn: un- 加 fair：fair 是持平的秤，unfair 是被压了的秤。

normal.en: Fair itself meant beautiful first, then clean, then just.
normal.cn: fair 本义先是「美丽」，再是「洁净」，后是「公正」。

normal.en: Fair and fare sound the same but fare only travels and pays.
normal.cn: fair 与 fare 同音，但 fare 只管出行与车费。

normal.en: The un- family: unhappy, unfair, unfit, unable.
normal.cn: un- 词族：unhappy、unfair、unfit、unable。

normal.en: Unfairly tells how, unfairness names the thing.
normal.cn: unfairly 说明方式，unfairness 给不公命名。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale with one pan secretly heavier.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，其中一侧托盘被悄悄加重了。

abstract.en: Un- tilts the level field until the ball rolls to one side.
abstract.cn: un- 把平整的场地一端抬起，球便滚向一侧。

abstract.en: Fairness is everyone's shoes on the same starting line.
abstract.cn: 公平就是所有人的鞋都落在同一条起跑线上。

examples.en: Changing the rules halfway through is unfair to every player.
examples.cn: 比赛进行到一半改规则，对每位选手都不公平。

examples.en: She complained of unfair treatment at work and won her case.
examples.cn: 她投诉在工作中受到不公平对待并胜诉。

examples.en: Critics called the tax unfair to small businesses.
examples.cn: 批评者称这项税对小企业不公平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安·费尔」——安（un 不）费尔（fair 公平）：不安逸的公平，即不公

root: unfair 由古英语否定前缀 un- 加 fair 构成；fair 溯自古英语 fæge「美丽的；注定一死的」，一般上溯至原始印欧语重构词根 *peh₂-（更早来源不确定）；词义由「美丽」经「洁净、合法」演化为「持中、公正」；un- 与拉丁语 in-、希腊语 a(n)- 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unfair all break one image: the level scale. Unequal treatment, favouritism, rule-breaking, undue advantage, bad procedure — each is a thumb pressed on one pan.
sensesIntro.cn: unfair 的八个义项都在破坏同一意象：那架持平的秤。不平等对待、偏袒、违规、不当优势、程序失当——每一条都是压在秤盘上的拇指。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance scale with a hidden weight on one pan
core.cn: 核心意象：一架秤，一侧托盘藏着看不见的砝码

branches.en: THE SCALE: unequal treatment, wrong weights, and favouritism.
branches.cn: 天平线：不平等对待、放错的砝码与偏袒。

branches.en: THE GAME: broken rules and advantages no rival shares.
branches.cn: 赛场线：被打破的规则与对手没有的优势。

branches.en: THE MARKET: improper conduct in the fair ring of trade.
branches.cn: 市场线：公平交易圈中的不正当行为。

branches.en: THE WORDS: blame that outweighs the deed.
branches.cn: 言辞线：重过行为本身的指责。

branches.en: THE COURT: procedures whose pivot itself has moved.
branches.cn: 法庭线：支点本身已移动的程序。

intro.en: Unfair shows the most productive negative pattern in English: un- on a native adjective.
intro.cn: unfair 展示了英语中最能产的否定模式：un- 加于本族形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 词基属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它与 partial 构成 impartial。

definition_zh: 足够的；适当的；胜任的；尚可的
definition_en: enough in amount for a purpose, good enough in quality or ability, or only just at the level required
core_image: 水正好倒到刻度线，不高也不低
scene: 宿舍楼的自习室里只剩角落一盏旧灯，翻开书还能看清字。 The old lamp gave just adequate light for reading.
sceneCN: 这里 adequate 指光线只到够用的程度（第 4 个义项：尚可、勉强够用）；句意为那盏旧灯提供的光勉强够看书。

pos.zh: 形容词：足够的；适当的；胜任的；尚可的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「足够；适当；胜任」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「足够地；适当地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「不足的；不适当的」
由 inadequate 加后缀 -acy 构成，义为「不足；欠缺」

senses.title: Enough in amount
senses.definition: existing in a quantity large enough for a particular need or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到足以满足某种需要或目的
senses.example: The shelter provides adequate food and clean water for every family.
senses.exampleCN: 收容所为每个家庭提供足够的食物和干净的水。
senses.why: Latin adaequatus means made equal: the amount is brought up to the level that the need sets, so it is enough but says nothing more.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adaequatus 意为「被弄得相等」：数量被提到需求所划出的那条线上，不多不少，所以是「足够」，并不涉及好坏。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: of a standard that is good enough for a purpose, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 达到足以满足某一目的的标准，但算不上出色
senses.example: The room was small but adequate for two guests.
senses.exampleCN: 房间不大，但接待两位客人足够了。
senses.why: Equal to a line can be said of quality as well as quantity: if the standard is met, the thing is adequate, no matter how plain it is.
senses.whyCN: 「与一条线齐平」既可以衡量数量，也可以衡量质量：只要达到标准就算 adequate，东西再普通也没关系。

senses.title: Competent for a role
senses.definition: of a person, having the ability or training needed for a task or position
senses.definitionCN: 指人具备完成某项任务或担任某个职位所需的能力或训练
senses.example: After a month of training, she was adequate to the job.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个月培训，她已能胜任这份工作。
senses.why: Put the same equality on a person: ability and the demands of the post meet at the line, and that meeting is what competence means here.
senses.whyCN: 把「相等」用到人身上，就是能力与岗位要求在那条线上相交；两者齐平，就是这里说的「胜任」。

senses.title: Barely sufficient
senses.definition: only just at the level required, with no margin of comfort or excellence
senses.definitionCN: 刚好达到要求，没有余量，也谈不上好
senses.example: His performance was adequate, but nobody praised it.
senses.exampleCN: 他的表现尚可，却没人称赞。
senses.why: This sense keeps the tightest edge of 'equal': the thing only touches the line and goes not one step beyond, which gives the word its faintly cool tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了「相等」最紧的一面：只碰到那条线，一步也不多，因此这个词常带一点冷淡的「勉强及格」语气。

intro.en: Adequate is a Latin participle built on aequus 'level, equal'; its history is the idea of bringing something up to a line.
intro.cn: adequate 是建立在 aequus「平的、相等的」之上的拉丁语分词，它的历史就是「把某物提到某条线上」这一想法。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal', and it also lies behind equal, equity and equator.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均匀的、相等的」，equal、equity 与 equator 也出自它。

items.en: Aequare 'to make level or equal' is the verb formed from aequus.
items.cn: aequare 意为「使平整、使相等」，是由 aequus 构成的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus aequare formed adaequare, 'to make equal to, bring up to a level'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 aequare 构成 adaequare，意为「使与……相等、提到同一水平」。

items.en: The past participle adaequatus meant 'made equal, equal to', and English took the adjective from it.
items.cn: 过去分词 adaequatus 意为「被弄得相等的、与……相等的」，英语由此借入形容词。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century, first in the sense of equal to a requirement; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪进入英语，最早表示「与要求相等」，确切的开始年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the word and one Latin cousin; the near-meaning group gathers words for enough, for acceptable, and for ability.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的各个形式与一个拉丁同族词；近义组收表示「足够」「合格」与「有能力」的词。

entries.definition: The state of being enough or good enough for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「足够、适当、胜任」，由本词加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: Not enough, or not good enough for what is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不足的、不适当的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A lack of something needed, or a failure to be good enough.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不足、欠缺」，由 inadequate 加后缀 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: To treat two things as equal; built on the same Latin root aequus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「把……等同看待」，与本词同出拉丁语 aequus「相等的」，是同根词而非派生词。

entries.definition: Enough for a stated purpose, in a more formal and precise tone than adequate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的」，语气比 adequate 更正式，也更强调正好满足某个目的。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the needed amount; it carries no judgement of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「足够的」，是最日常的说法，完全不涉及质量好坏。

entries.definition: Good enough to be accepted, with the emphasis on meeting someone's approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的、合格的」，重点在于达到他人的认可。

entries.definition: Having enough skill for a task; used of people rather than of amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的、称职的」，只用于人或其表现，不用于数量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root aequus 'level, equal' and the two fixed patterns adequate for and adequate to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 aequus「平的、相等的」，以及 adequate for 与 adequate to 两个固定结构。

normal.en: Adequate is ad- 'to' plus aequus 'equal': something is adequate when it is brought up to the level needed.
normal.cn: adequate 是 ad-「朝向」加 aequus「相等」：把某物提到所需的高度，它就是 adequate。

normal.en: Aequus also gives equal and equity; all of them keep the image of a level line.
normal.cn: aequus 还给出 equal 与 equity，它们都保留了「同一条水平线」的画面。

normal.en: Adequate says nothing about excellence: it only says that the line has been reached.
normal.cn: adequate 完全不谈出色，它只说明那条线已经够到了。

normal.en: Adequate for a purpose and adequate to a task are the two patterns worth memorising.
normal.cn: adequate for 接目的，adequate to 接任务，这两个结构最值得记。

normal.en: The opposite is inadequate, made with the negative prefix in-.
normal.cn: 反义词是 inadequate，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water filled exactly to a pencilled line, no drop above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水正好倒到铅笔画的那条线上，一滴也不多。

abstract.en: Imagine three marks on a wall: below the line is inadequate, on the line is adequate, far above it is excellent.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上有三道刻度：线以下是不足，压线是够用，远远高出才是出色。

abstract.en: The same line measures rice, a room and a person's skill, which is why one adjective covers all three.
abstract.cn: 同一条线既量米、量房间，也量一个人的本事，所以一个形容词能同时管这三件事。

examples.en: The shelter provides adequate food and clean water for every family.
examples.cn: 收容所为每个家庭提供足够的食物和干净的水。

examples.en: The room was small but adequate for two guests.
examples.cn: 房间不大，但接待两位客人足够了。

examples.en: After a month of training, she was adequate to the job.
examples.cn: 经过一个月培训，她已能胜任这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德夸特」——阿德把水倒到刻度线就停手：够用就好，不多不少。

root: 拉丁语 adaequatus「被弄得相等的」，源自 adaequare「使与……相等」，由 ad-「朝向」+ aequare「使平整、使相等」构成；aequus「平的、相等的」是它的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses of adequate all measure something against a line: an amount, a standard of quality, a person's ability, or the bare minimum.
sensesIntro.cn: adequate 的四个义项都在拿某物去比对一条线：数量、质量标准、人的能力，或最低限度的及格线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water poured up to a marked line, no higher and no lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：水正好倒到刻度线，不高也不低。

branches.en: AMOUNT: the line marks how much is needed, and the supply reaches it exactly.
branches.cn: 数量线：刻度标出需要多少，供给正好到达那里。

branches.en: QUALITY: the same line applied to a standard means acceptable, not excellent.
branches.cn: 质量线：同一条线用来衡量标准，就是合格而不出色。

branches.en: PERSON: ability and the demands of a post meet at the line, and the person is competent.
branches.cn: 人线：能力与岗位要求在那条线上相交，人就能胜任。

branches.en: MINIMUM: the thing only touches the line, and that tightness gives the word its cool tone.
branches.cn: 最低线：只碰到那条线，这种紧贴感让这个词带上冷淡的语气。

branches.en: SHARED IMAGE: whether the object is rice or a room, the judgement is the same act of levelling.
branches.cn: 共同画面：不管对象是一袋米还是一间房，判断都是同一个「找齐」的动作。

intro.en: Adequate is a Latin participle; English builds its noun, adverb and negative with ordinary endings.
intro.cn: adequate 是一个拉丁语分词，英语用普通词尾构成它的名词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Aequus, aequare and adaequatus are all recorded in Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root of aequus is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: aequus、aequare 与 adaequatus 在拉丁语中均有记录，只有 aequus 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It adds the idea of reaching a point.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「抵达某一点」的意思。

items.example: Aequus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aequus 是这一词族的词根。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an action.

items.meaning: to make equal to, bring up to a level
items.meaningCN: 使与……相等；提到同一水平
items.example: It joins the prefix with the verb of levelling.
items.exampleCN: 它把前缀与表示「找平」的动词合在一起。

items.example: English borrowed it as the adjective adequate.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它借来作形容词 adequate。

definition_zh: 活动人士；积极分子；维权者；激进推动变革的人
definition_en: a person who works actively to bring about political or social change, often outside formal positions of power
core_image: 街口举着纸牌的人：要把自己的想法推到众人眼前
scene: 清晨的市政厅台阶上，几个人举着写满字的纸牌，安静地站成一排。 A group of activists waited outside city hall with hand-painted signs.
sceneCN: 这里 activist 指「为公共议题公开行动的人」（第 1 个义项：社会议题的活动人士）；句意为一群活动人士举着手写标语在市政厅外等候。

pos.zh: 名词：活动人士；积极分子；维权者
形容词（作定语）：激进推动变革的

collocations.zh: 积极介入公司经营的投资人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「行动主义；社会运动」
由本词加形容词后缀 -istic 构成，义为「行动主义的；积极介入的」
由前缀 anti- 加本词构成，义为「反对活动人士的」

senses.title: A campaigner for social change
senses.definition: a person who works publicly to bring about political or social change
senses.definitionCN: 公开为政治或社会变革而努力的人
senses.example: She became a human rights activist while still at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她还在读大学时就成了一名人权活动人士。
senses.why: The Latin root agere means to drive or do, and -ist marks the person who does, so an activist is literally one who keeps driving a cause forward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 agere 意为「驱动、做」，-ist 标记做这件事的人；activist 字面上就是不断把一项事业往前推的人。

senses.title: An active member of a party or union
senses.titleCN: 政党或工会里的积极分子
senses.definition: a member of a party, union or similar body who works hard for it at local level
senses.definitionCN: 在政党、工会等团体基层努力做事的成员
senses.example: Every branch needs a few activists to knock on doors before the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举前每个支部都需要几个积极分子去挨家敲门。
senses.why: The doer suffix narrows to organizational life: the activist is the member who does the unglamorous work inside a group.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示「做事者」的后缀收窄到组织生活里：activist 是团体内部做那些不出彩实事的人。

senses.title: An advocate for a single cause
senses.definition: a person who campaigns on one particular issue, such as the environment or animal welfare
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某一个特定议题开展倡导的人，如环保或动物福利
senses.example: Local activists have opposed the new road for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 当地的活动人士反对这条新路已经三年了。
senses.why: Once a cause becomes the thing being driven, the driver is named after it, so we say environmental activist or animal activist.
senses.whyCN: 当某个议题成为被推动的对象，推动者就以它命名，于是有了环保活动人士、动物保护活动人士这样的说法。

senses.title: Someone who takes direct action
senses.definition: a person who joins protests, blockades or occupations instead of working only through institutions
senses.definitionCN: 参加抗议、封锁或占领行动的人，而不只是走机构渠道
senses.example: The activists chained themselves to the gate at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那些行动者在黎明时把自己锁在了大门上。
senses.why: If agere is to drive forward, the most physical form of driving is a body placed in the way.
senses.whyCN: 如果说 agere 是「向前驱动」，最物理的驱动形式就是把身体挡在路上。

senses.title: A campaigner organizing online
senses.definition: a person who builds support and pressure through social media and online networks
senses.definitionCN: 借助社交媒体和网络组织支持、施加压力的人
senses.example: A student activist turned a hashtag into a nationwide campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 一名学生活动分子把一个标签话题变成了全国性的运动。
senses.why: The driving now happens through shares and posts, but the medium changes while the doer stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 驱动如今通过转发和发帖完成；媒介变了，做事的人却没有变。

senses.title: An investor pressing for corporate change
senses.titleCN: 积极介入经营的投资人
senses.definition: in finance, an investor who buys a large stake and pushes a company to change its strategy or management
senses.definitionCN: 金融语境中买下大量股份、推动公司改变战略或管理层的投资人
senses.example: The board gave in after an activist investor bought a large stake.
senses.exampleCN: 一名积极介入的投资人买下大量股份后，董事会作出了让步。
senses.why: The word moves into markets: the thing being driven is no longer a cause but a company.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入了市场：被推动的对象不再是某项事业，而是一家公司。

senses.title: Used before a noun: pushing for change
senses.titleCN: 作定语：主张激进变革的
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe a group, policy or court that actively pushes for change instead of preserving things as they are
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，形容某个团体、政策或法院积极推动变革，而非维持现状
senses.example: The group took its case to an activist court.
senses.exampleCN: 该团体把案子送到了以推动变革著称的法院。
senses.why: As a modifier the word sheds the person and keeps the force, so the pushing itself becomes the quality described.
senses.whyCN: 作定语时这个词卸下了「人」的身份却保留了力度：推动本身成了被描述的性质。

senses.title: A critical label for judges
senses.titleCN: 贬义标签：所谓「司法能动」的
senses.definition: in political debate, a critical label for judges said to make policy instead of applying the law
senses.definitionCN: 政治争论中带有批评意味的标签，指被指控制定政策而非适用法律的法官
senses.example: Critics called the ruling the work of activist judges.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这项裁决出自所谓「司法能动」的法官之手。
senses.why: The same force praised in a campaigner is blamed in a judge: driving change where the critic thinks none should be driven.
senses.whyCN: 活动人士身上被赞许的那股推动力，落到法官身上就成了指责：在批评者看来，本不该推动的地方却被推动了。

intro.en: Activist is an English formation on the Latin verb agere, with a Greek-derived person suffix; the family is old, the word itself recent.
intro.cn: activist 是在拉丁语动词 agere 基础上构成的英语词，配上一个源自希腊语的人物后缀；词族古老，这个词本身却很晚。

items.en: *ag- is generally reconstructed as 'to drive, set in motion'. The deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ag- 表示「驱动、使运动」；这个更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The verb agere meant 'to drive, lead, do, act', and its past participle was actus.
items.cn: 动词 agere 意为「驱动、引领、做、行动」，其过去分词是 actus。

items.en: The noun actus meant 'a driving, a doing, an act'; English drew act and action from this branch.
items.cn: 名词 actus 意为「驱动、作为、行为」；英语的 act 与 action 都取自这一支。

items.en: Act entered English from Latin and Old French, first naming a deed, then the doing of it.
items.cn: act 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，最初指一件做过的事，后来也指做的过程。

items.en: Activist joins act to the suffix -ist, which came from Greek -istes through Latin -ista. The word is recorded from the early twentieth century and spread with mass political movements.
items.cn: activist 由 act 加后缀 -ist 构成，这一后缀从希腊语经拉丁语进入英语。该词二十世纪初已有记录，并随大众政治运动而流行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same driving root; the near-meaning group gathers people who press for change in different ways.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「驱动」词根的一族词；近义组收以不同方式推动改变的人。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of activists, formed with the suffix -ism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动主义、社会运动」，由本词加后缀 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: The root verb and noun meaning to do something or a thing done.
entries.definitionCN: 动词兼名词，义为「行动、行为」，是这一词族的基础词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning taking action rather than waiting; it stands behind activist.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「积极的、活跃的」，是 activist 的直接来源之一。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to set something going, literally to make it act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「启动、激活」，字面就是「使其行动」。

entries.definition: A person who makes art; it merely looks close and comes from Latin ars, not from agere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「艺术家」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，出自拉丁语 ars。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an organized campaign, often with a formal group behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运动参与者、竞选者」，往往背后有正式组织。

entries.definition: A person who shows public disagreement, especially at a demonstration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抗议者」，尤指在示威现场公开表达反对的人。

entries.definition: A person who publicly supports a cause, often by speaking and writing rather than acting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡导者」，多靠言论与写作支持某项主张。

entries.definition: A person who joins a march or rally; the emphasis is on the event, not on a long campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「示威者」，强调参加某场游行集会，而非长期运动。

entries.definition: A person paid to persuade politicians, working inside the system rather than in the street.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「说客」，受雇游说政客，走体制内渠道而非街头。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the person suffix and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子借助真实的拉丁词根、人物后缀，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Act is the root: an activist is someone who acts rather than watches.
normal.cn: act 是词根：activist 就是去做而不是旁观的人。

normal.en: The suffix -ist marks a person, as in artist or scientist; here the person drives a cause.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ist 标记人，如 artist、scientist；在这里，这个人推动的是一项事业。

normal.en: Activism is the activity, and activist is the person who carries it out.
normal.cn: activism 指这项活动，activist 指从事它的人。

normal.en: Environmental activist and human rights activist are the two commonest patterns.
normal.cn: environmental activist 与 human rights activist 是最常见的两种搭配。

normal.en: In finance an activist investor pushes a company; the same word, a different arena.
normal.cn: 在金融里，activist investor 推动一家公司；同一个词，换了个场域。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a heavy door: the door is the old rule, the hand is the activist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在推一扇沉重的门：门是旧规矩，手就是活动人士。

abstract.en: A sign held above a crowd works like a small sail catching a large wind.
abstract.cn: 人群中举起的标语，像一面小帆接住了一阵大风。

abstract.en: The pushing can be praised or blamed; what stays constant is that someone refuses to stand still.
abstract.cn: 这股推动力可能被赞许，也可能被指责；不变的是有人拒绝原地站着。

examples.en: Local activists have been pressing the council for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 当地的活动人士一直在要求市议会改善空气质量。

examples.en: She works as a climate activist while holding a full-time job.
examples.cn: 她一边做全职工作，一边从事气候运动。

examples.en: The board gave in after an activist investor bought a large stake.
examples.cn: 一名积极介入的投资人买下大量股份后，董事会作出了让步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克提维斯特」——爱把问题「提」到台面上的人：活动人士。

root: 由 act 加后缀 -ist 构成；act 出自拉丁语 agere「驱动、做」的过去分词 actus，-ist 源自希腊语 -istes，经拉丁语 -ista 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses name the same pushing force: a person who drives a cause, a party, a single issue, a protest, a network, a company, or a court.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项指的是同一股推动力：推动一项事业、一个政党、一个单一议题、一场抗议、一张网络、一家公司，或一座法院的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holding a sign at a street corner, pushing an idea into public view.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角一个举着标语的人，把一个想法推到公众眼前。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the doer suffix turns the drive into a person who keeps a cause moving.
branches.cn: 人物线：表示做事者的后缀把「驱动」变成一个人，他让一项事业持续向前。

branches.en: THE GROUP: inside a party or an online network, the same doer does the everyday work of organizing.
branches.cn: 团体线：无论在政党里还是在网络里，同一个做事者承担着日常的组织工作。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: a single issue becomes the thing driven, and the driver takes its name.
branches.cn: 议题线：单一议题成为被推动之物，推动者便以它命名。

branches.en: THE STREET: the most physical driving is a body placed in the way.
branches.cn: 街头线：最物理的驱动，是把身体挡在路上。

branches.en: THE MARKET AND THE COURT: the same force is hired in an investor, described in a policy, and blamed in a judge.
branches.cn: 市场与法庭线：同一股力量，在投资人身上被雇用，在政策上被描述，在法官身上被指责。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root plus an English noun and adjective pattern; the suffixes below build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加上英语的名词与形容词构词方式；下面这些后缀撑起了整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Agere, actus and actio are recorded Latin forms; the Indo-European root above them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere、actus、actio 都是有文献记录的拉丁语形式；更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。
